components.name: A01NYUB Waterproof Ultrasonic Sensor
components.description: This sensor allows you to use A01NYUB waterproof ultrasonic sensor by DFRobot ([datasheet](https://wiki.dfrobot.com/A01NYUB%20Waterproof%20Ultrasonic%20Sensor%20SKU_SEN0313)) with ESPHome to measure distances. This sensor can measure ranges between 28 centimeters and 750 centimeters with a resolution of 1 millimeter.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the sensor. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default device class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: Uart Id
config_entries.description: The ID of the [UART bus](https://esphome.io/components/uart) you wish to use for this sensor. Use this if you want to use multiple UART buses at once.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.description: The state class for the sensor. components.name: Stepper Component
components.description: Put this code into the configuration file on ESPHome for this device.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Specify the ID of the stepper so that you can control it.

config_entries.label: Dir Pin
config_entries.description: The `DIRECTION` pin of the A4988 stepper driver.

config_entries.label: Max Speed
config_entries.description: The maximum speed in `steps/s` (steps per seconds) to drive the stepper at. Note most steppers can't step properly with speeds higher than 250 steps/s.

config_entries.label: Sleep Pin
config_entries.description: Optionally also use the `SLEEP` pin of the A4988 stepper driver. If specified, the driver will be put into sleep mode as soon as the stepper reaches the target steps.

config_entries.label: Step Pin
config_entries.description: The `STEP` pin of the A4988 stepper driver.

config_entries.label: Acceleration
config_entries.description: The acceleration in `steps/s^2` (steps per seconds squared) to use when starting to move. The default is `inf` which means infinite acceleration, so the stepper will try to drive with the full speed immediately. This value is helpful if that first motion of the motor is too jerky for what it's moving. If you make this a small number, it will take the motor a moment to get up to speed.

config_entries.label: Deceleration
config_entries.description: The same as `acceleration`, but for when the motor is decelerating shortly before reaching the set position. Defaults to `inf` (immediate deceleration).

components.name: ADE7880 Power Sensor
components.description: The `ade7880` sensor platform allows you to use ADE7880 voltage/current/power sensors ([datasheet](https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ADE7880.pdf)) with ESPHome. This sensor chip is commonly found in Shelly 3EM and 3EM Pro devices.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to report the sensor values. Defaults to `60s`.

config_entries.label: Irq0 Pin
config_entries.description: The GPIO pin that the ADE7880's IRQ0 output is connected to, if any. The `ade7880` component does not use this input, but if the IRQ0 output is connected to a GPIO and that GPIO is *not* configured as an `input`, the chip will produce excessive heat and its lifetime could be shortened. The simplest way to ensure that the GPIO pin is properly connected is to supply it here, but if you wish to configure it elsewhere in your configuration that is a reasonable alternative.

config_entries.label: Irq1 Pin
config_entries.description: The GPIO pin that the ADE7880's IRQ1 output is connected to. The `ade7880` component uses this input to determine when the ADE7880 chip has completed its power-up and reset cycles.

config_entries.label: Reset Pin
config_entries.description: The GPIO pin that the ADE7880's RESET input is connected to, if any. If this pin is configured, the `ade7880` component will use it to initiate a 'hardware reset' of the chip when needed; if this pin is not configured, the component will attempt to initiate a 'software reset' of the chip when needed, but this could fail if the chip is not responding properly to the I2C bus.

config_entries.label: I2C Id
config_entries.description: Specify the ID of the [I2C Component](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) if your configuration includes multiple I2C buses.

config_entries.label: Frequency
config_entries.description: The AC line frequency of the supply voltage. The supported range is `45Hz` to `66Hz`. Defaults to `50Hz`.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the phase, which will be used a prefix in the names of all of the phase's sensors.

config_entries.label: Calibration

config_entries.description: The path (relative to where the .yaml file is) of the gif file.

config_entries.label: Loop
config_entries.description: If you want to loop over a subset of your animation (e.g. a fire animation where the fire "starts", then "burns" and "dies") you can specify some frames to loop over.

config_entries.label: End Frame
config_entries.description: The last frame to show in the loop; when this frame is reached it will loop back to `start_frame`. Defaults to the last frame in the animation.

config_entries.label: Repeat
config_entries.description: Specifies how many times the loop will run. When the count is reached, the animation will continue with the next frame after `end_frame`, or restart from the beginning if `end_frame` was the last frame. Defaults to "loop forever".

config_entries.label: Start Frame
config_entries.description: The frame to loop back to when `end_frame` is reached. Defaults to the first frame in the animation.

config_entries.label: Resize
config_entries.description: If set, this will resize all the frames to fit inside the given dimensions `WIDTHxHEIGHT` and preserve the aspect ratio.

config_entries.label: Transparency
config_entries.description: If set the alpha channel of the input image will be taken into account. The possible values are `opaque` (default), `chroma_key` and `alpha_channel`. See discussion on transparency in the [image component](https://esphome.io/components/image#display-image).

config_entries.label: Irq Pin
config_entries.description: The IRQ pin, which indicates if a lightning strike has been detected.

config_entries.label: Calibration
config_entries.description: Enable/disable oscillator calibration on startup. It is recommended to perform antenna tuning procedure first and adjust parameters, so that RLC antenna resonance is tuned within optimal range. Defaults to `True`.

config_entries.label: Capacitance
config_entries.description: This setting will add capacitance to the series RLC antenna on the product to help tune its resonance. The datasheet specifies being within 3.5 percent of 500kHz to get optimal lightning detection and distance sensing. It's possible to add up to 120pF in steps of 8pF to the antenna. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Div Ratio
config_entries.description: The antenna is designed to resonate at 500kHz and so can be tuned with the following setting. The accuracy of the antenna must be within 3.5 percent of that value for proper signal validation and distance estimation. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Indoor
config_entries.description: Indicates if the sensor is used indoor. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Lightning Threshold
config_entries.description: The number of lightnings that must appear in a 15-minute time window before a lightning storm is detected. 15 minutes is the window of time before the number of detected lightning events is reset. The number of lightning strikes can be set to 1,5,9, or 16. Defaults to `1`.

config_entries.label: Mask Disturber
config_entries.description: This setting will return whether or not disturbers trigger the IRQ Pin. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Noise Level
config_entries.description: Noise floor level is compared to known reference voltage. If this level is exceeded the chip will issue an interrupt to the IRQ pin, broadcasting that it can not operate properly due to noise (INT_NH). Defaults to `2`.

config_entries.label: Spike Rejection
config_entries.description: Helps to differentiate between false events and actual lightning. Increasing this value increases robustness at the cost of sensitivity to distant events. Defaults to `2`.

config_entries.label: Tune Antenna
config_entries.description: Start sensor in antenna tuning mode. It will emit oscillator frequency to be read on the INT pin. Please follow AS3935 documentation. Note that while this mode is enabled, lightings will not be detected. It should be used for initial calibration only, in order to determine correct value of `capacitance` and/or `div_ratio` parameters. Defaults to `False`.

config_entries.label: Watchdog Threshold
config_entries.description: Determines the threshold for events that trigger the IRQ pin. Defaults to `2`.

components.name: AirTouch AT581x Radar
components.description: The [AirTouch AT581x radar](https://en.airtouching.com/product/32.html) (aka `AT581x`  ) is a family of 5.8GHz radar which can be used for human presence detection. It can detect tiny movements and compared to a PIR sensor **it can detect presence continuously**. This can be useful, for example, to turn the lights on when you enter a room, keep them on as long as you are there (without waving your hands at the sensor) and turn them off almost immediately after you leave the room.

components.name: ATM90E26 Power Sensor
components.description: The `atm90e26` sensor platform allows you to use your ATM90E26 voltage/current and power sensors ([datasheet](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/Atmel-46002-SE-M90E26-Datasheet.pdf)) with ESPHome. This sensor is found in the [DitroniX GTEM ESP32](https://ditronix.net/wiki/gtem-esp32-atm90e26-sdk-v1-specification/) energy meter and other devices.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to check the sensor. Defaults to `60s`.

config_entries.label: Cs Pin
config_entries.description: The pin CS is connected to. For the 6 channel meter main board, this will always be 5 and 4. For the add-on boards a jumper can be selected for each CS pin, but default to 0 and 16.

config_entries.label: Line Frequency
config_entries.description: The AC line frequency of the supply voltage. One of `50Hz`, `60Hz`.

config_entries.label: Meter Constant
config_entries.description: The number of pulses per kWh. The ATM90E26 internally works based on pulses and this value converts a pulse into Wh, which are emitted as `forward_active_energy` etc. Matching it against an existing meter is useful in that it allows visual confirmation for some devices that blink an LED for each pulse. Common values are 1000 pulses/kWh, 1666.66 pulses/kWh, or 3200 pulses/kWh. See also **gain_metering** which determines after how much energy a pulse is emitted.

With multiple ATM90E32 sensors each one is enabled individually, and it's buttons are mapped using an id value pair. e.g. `id: chip1` when more than one is defined. After running, the values are stored in chip memory and will be available upon reboot and OTA software updates.

config_entries.label: Enable Offset Calibration
config_entries.description: If true this enables fine grained offset noise 0 level calibration for voltage, `offset_voltage`, and current sensors, `offset_current`, & power offset for active, `offset_active_power`, and reactive power, `offset_reactive_power`. Buttons are required to operate the calibration feature. With multiple ATM90E32 sensors each one is enabled individually, and it's buttons are mapped using an id value pair. e.g. `id: chip1` when more than one is defined. After running, the values are stored in chip memory and will be available upson reboot and OTA software updates. Offset calibration can only be performed when all voltage and current inputs are at a 0 value. USB power is recommended. For power offset calibration, only a voltage transformer should be connected.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Debug Prefix
config_entries.description: Prefix prepended to every debug log line. Useful when multiple UART buses log at the same time.

config_entries.label: Dummy Receiver
config_entries.description: Capture incoming bytes even when no UART device component is bound to the bus. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: After
config_entries.description: When to flush accumulated bytes to the log.

config_entries.label: Bytes
config_entries.description: Flush after this many bytes have been accumulated. Defaults to 150.

config_entries.label: Timeout
config_entries.description: Flush after no bytes have been seen for this long. Defaults to `100ms`.

config_entries.label: Delimiter
config_entries.description: Flush as soon as this byte sequence is seen in the stream.

config_entries.label: Rx Buffer Size
config_entries.description: Size of the receive buffer in bytes. Range: 160-8192. Defaults to `512`. Valid only for mode `uart`.

config_entries.label: Tx Buffer Size
config_entries.description: Size of the transmit buffer in bytes. Range: 160-8192. Defaults to `512`.

config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. config_entries.label: Ibeacon Major
config_entries.description: The iBeacon major identifier of the beacon that needs to be tracked. Usually used to group beacons, for example for grouping all beacons in the same building.

config_entries.label: Ibeacon Minor
config_entries.description: The iBeacon minor identifier of the beacon that needs to be tracked. Usually used to identify beacons within an iBeacon group.

config_entries.label: Ibeacon Uuid
config_entries.description: The [universally unique identifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universally_unique_identifier) to identify the beacon that needs to be tracked. Note that exactly one of `mac_address`, `irk`, `service_uuid` or `ibeacon_uuid` must be present.

config_entries.label: Irk
config_entries.description: The Identity Resolving Key (IRK) to track for this sensor. Note that exactly one of `mac_address`, `irk`, `service_uuid` or `ibeacon_uuid` must be present.

config_entries.label: Mac Address
config_entries.description: The MAC address to track for this sensor. Note that exactly one of `mac_address`, `irk`, `service_uuid` or `ibeacon_uuid` must be present.

config_entries.label: Service Uuid
config_entries.description: The BLE Service UUID which can be tracked if the device randomizes the MAC address. Note that exactly one of `mac_address`, `irk`, `service_uuid` or `ibeacon_uuid` must be present.

components.name: Bluetooth Proxy
components.description: Home Assistant can expand its Bluetooth reach by communicating through the Bluetooth proxy component in ESPHome. The individual device integrations in Home Assistant (such as BTHome) will receive the data from the Bluetooth Integration in Home Assistant which automatically aggregates all ESPHome Bluetooth proxies with any USB Bluetooth Adapters you might have. components.description: You first need to set up the [I2C](https://esphome.io/components/i2c/) component.

config_entries.description: Manually specify the I²C address of the RTC. Defaults to `0x51`.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: How often to synchronize the device time from the source. Defaults to `15min`.

config_entries.description: Specify the ID of the time for use in lambdas.

config_entries.label: Timezone
config_entries.description: Manually tell ESPHome what time zone to use with [this format](https://www.gnu.org/software/libc/manual/html_node/TZ-Variable.html) (warning: the format is quite complicated, see [examples](https://github.com/nayarsystems/posix_tz_db/blob/master/zones.csv)) or the simpler [TZ database name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones) in the form `<Region>/<City>`. ESPHome tries to automatically infer the time zone string based on the time zone of the computer that is running ESPHome, but this might not always be accurate. Not available on nRF52 platforms.

components.name: BME680 Temperature+Pressure+Humidity+Gas Sensor via BSEC
components.description: The `bme680_bsec` sensor platform allows you to use your BME680 ([datasheet](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/media/boschsensortec/downloads/datasheets/bst-bme680-ds001.pdf), [Adafruit](https://www.adafruit.com/product/3660), [Pimoroni](https://shop.pimoroni.com/products/bme680-breakout)) temperature, pressure and humidity and gas sensors with ESPHome via the Bosch Sensortec Environmental Cluster (BSEC) software library. The use of Bosch's proprietary algorithms provide an Index for Air Quality (IAQ) measurement derived from the gas resistance sensor's response to specific Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC). The BSEC software also provides estimated values for CO₂ and Breath Volatile Organic Compounds (b-VOC) using a correlation between VOC and CO₂ in a human's exhaled breath.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: Manually specify the I²C address of the sensor. Defaults to `0x76`. Another address can be `0x77`.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation. Use this ID in the sensor section to refer to the correct BME680 if you have more than one device. This will also be used to refer to the calibrated BSEC algorithm state saved to flash.

config_entries.label: Iaq Mode
config_entries.description: IAQ calculation mode. Default is `static` for static applications (e.g. fixed indoor devices). Can be `mobile` for mobile applications (e.g. carry-on devices).

config_entries.label: Sample Rate
config_entries.description: Sample rate. Default is `lp` for low power consumption, sampling every 3 seconds. Can be `ulp` for ultra-low power, sampling every 5 minutes. This controls the sampling rate for gas-dependent sensors and will govern the interval at which the sensor heater is operated. By default, this rate will also be used for temperature, pressure, and humidity sensors but these can be overridden on a per-sensor level if required.

config_entries.label: State Save Interval
config_entries.description: The minimum interval at which to save calibrated BSEC algorithm state to flash so that calibration doesn't have to start from zero on device restart. Defaults to `6h`.

config_entries.label: Supply Voltage
config_entries.description: Supply voltage of the sensor. Default is `3.3V`. Can be set to `1.8V` if your sensor is 1.8V-powered (e.g. the Pimoroni PIM357 BME680 Breakout module).

config_entries.label: Temperature Offset
config_entries.description: Temperature offset if device is in enclosure and reads too high. This value is subtracted from the reading (e.g. if the sensor reads 5°C higher than expected, set this to `5`  ) and also corrects the relative humidity readings. Defaults to `0`.

components.name: Camera Encoder
components.description: The `camera_encoder` component provides image compression support for software-based cameras or cameras without internal compression. It allows raw camera frames to be compressed into a format suitable for transmission to API clients, such as Home Assistant, which expect JPEG-compressed images.

components.name: CAP1188 Capacitive Touch Sensor
components.description: The `cap1188` sensor platform allows you to use your CAP1188 ([datasheet](https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/datasheets/CAP1188.pdf), [Adafruit](https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-cap1188-breakout/overview)) Capacitive Touch Sensor with ESPHome. The [I²C](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) bus is required to be set up in your configuration for this sensor to work.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: The I²C address of the sensor. Defaults to `0x29`.

config_entries.label: Reset Pin
config_entries.description: Set the pin that is used to reset the CAP1188 board on boot.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Set the ID of this sensor.

config_entries.label: Allow Multiple Touches
config_entries.description: Whether to allow multitouch. Defaults to off.

config_entries.label: Touch Threshold
config_entries.description: The touch threshold for all channels. This defines the sensitivity for touch detection.

components.description: The `cap1188` binary sensor allows you to use your CAP1188 with ESPHome. First, setup a [Component/Hub](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/cap1188#cap1188-component) and then use this binary sensor platform to create individual binary sensors for each touch sensor.

components.name: Captive Portal
components.description: The captive portal component in ESPHome is a fallback mechanism for when connecting to the configured [WiFi](https://esphome.io/components/wifi/) fails.

config_entries.label: Compression
config_entries.description: The compression algorithm used for the embedded web assets. Options are `gzip` or `br` (Brotli). Brotli provides ~24% smaller size than gzip, but some browsers only support Brotli over HTTPS connections. Since the captive portal is served over HTTP, gzip is recommended for maximum compatibility. Defaults to `gzip`.

components.name: CC1101 Low-Power Sub-1 GHz RF Transceiver
components.description: The **CC1101** component provides a driver for the **Texas Instruments CC1101** Sub-1 GHz RF Transceiver ([datasheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/cc1101.pdf)). The CC1101 is a low-cost, low-power radio chip commonly used for wireless communication in the 300-928 MHz frequency bands, including the popular 315 MHz, 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz ISM bands.

config_entries.label: Cs Pin
config_entries.description: The SPI Chip Select (CSN) pin connected to the module.

config_entries.label: Gdo0 Pin
config_entries.description: The GDO0 pin. Required when `packet_mode` is enabled, also used for single pin mode switching.

config_entries.label: Carrier Sense Above Threshold
config_entries.description: Only accept packets when carrier sense indicates a signal is present. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Carrier Sense Abs Thr
config_entries.description: Absolute RSSI threshold for carrier sense. The radio considers a carrier present when RSSI exceeds this level. Range: `-8` to `7`.

config_entries.label: Carrier Sense Rel Thr
config_entries.description: Relative RSSI threshold for carrier sense, compared to the current noise floor. Options: `Default`, `+6dB`, `+10dB`, `+14dB`.

config_entries.label: Channel
config_entries.description: Channel number (added to base frequency). Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Channel Spacing
config_entries.description: Spacing between channels. Range: `25kHz` to `405kHz`. Defaults to `200kHz`.

config_entries.label: Crc Enable
config_entries.description: Enable CRC-16 calculation and checking. The CC1101 uses CRC-16-IBM (polynomial 0x8005). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Dc Blocking Filter
config_entries.description: Enable the digital DC blocking filter. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Filter Bandwidth
config_entries.description: The receive filter bandwidth. Range: `58kHz` to `812kHz`. Defaults to `203kHz`.

config_entries.label: Filter Length Ask Ook
config_entries.description: Averaging length for AGC in ASK/OOK modes. Longer values provide more stable gain but slower response. Options: `4dB`, `8dB`, `12dB`, `16dB`.

config_entries.label: Filter Length Fsk Msk
config_entries.description: Averaging length for AGC in FSK/MSK modes. Longer values provide more stable gain but slower response. Options: `8`, `16`, `32`, `64`.

config_entries.label: Freeze
config_entries.description: Controls when AGC gain is frozen (held constant). Options: `Default`, `On Sync`, `Analog Only`, `Analog And Digital`.

config_entries.label: Frequency
config_entries.description: The operating frequency. Range: `300MHz` to `928MHz`. Defaults to `433.92MHz`.

config_entries.label: Fsk Deviation
config_entries.description: Frequency deviation for FSK/GFSK modulation. Range: `1.5kHz` to `381kHz`.

config_entries.label: Hyst Level
config_entries.description: Hysteresis level to prevent gain oscillation on borderline signals. Options: `None`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High`.

config_entries.label: If Frequency
config_entries.description: Intermediate Frequency. Range: `25kHz` to `788kHz`. Defaults to `153kHz`.

config_entries.label: Lna Priority
config_entries.description: If true, reduce LNA gain before DVGA gain when decreasing overall gain. Useful for optimizing noise figure. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Magn Target
config_entries.description: Target signal amplitude for the AGC loop. Higher values increase sensitivity but may cause clipping on strong signals. Range: `24dB` to `42dB` in increments of 3 (e.g., `33dB`). Defaults to `42dB`.

config_entries.label: Manchester
config_entries.description: Enable Manchester encoding. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Max Dvga Gain
config_entries.description: Limits the maximum DVGA (Digital Variable Gain Amplifier) gain. Options: `Default`, `-1`, `-2`, `-3`. Defaults to `-3`.

config_entries.label: Max Lna Gain
config_entries.description: Limits the maximum LNA (Low Noise Amplifier) gain. Use to prevent saturation in high-signal environments. Defaults to `Default`. Options: `Default`, `2.6dB`, `6.1dB`, `7.4dB`, `9.2dB`, `11.5dB`, `14.6dB`, `17.1dB`.

config_entries.label: Modulation Type
config_entries.description: The modulation format. Options: `ASK/OOK` (default), `2-FSK`, `4-FSK`, `GFSK`, `MSK`.

config_entries.label: Msk Deviation
config_entries.description: Deviation index for MSK modulation. Range: `1` to `8`.

config_entries.label: Num Preamble
config_entries.description: Number of preamble bytes to transmit. Range: `0` to `7` (maps to 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24 bytes). Defaults to `2` (4 bytes).

config_entries.label: Output Power
config_entries.description: The transmission power in dBm. Range: `-30` to `11`. Defaults to `10`.

config_entries.label: Packet Length
config_entries.description: Packet length in bytes. Set to `0` for variable length packets (length byte prepended to data). Range: `0` to `64`. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Packet Mode
config_entries.description: Enable FIFO packet mode. When enabled, `gdo0_pin` is required. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Rx Attenuation
config_entries.description: Internal RX attenuation. Options: `0dB`, `6dB`, `12dB`, `18dB`. Defaults to `0dB`.

config_entries.label: Symbol Rate
config_entries.description: The symbol rate in Baud. Range: `600` to `500000`. Defaults to `5000`.

config_entries.label: Sync0
config_entries.description: Lower sync word byte. Defaults to `0x91`.

config_entries.label: Sync1
config_entries.description: Upper sync word byte. Defaults to `0xD3`.

config_entries.label: Sync Mode
config_entries.description: Sync word detection mode. Options: `None`, `15/16`, `16/16`, `30/32`. Defaults to `16/16`.

config_entries.label: Wait Time
config_entries.description: Time to wait after a gain change before allowing another adjustment. Options: `8`, `16`, `24`, `32`. Defaults to `32`.

config_entries.label: Whitening
config_entries.description: Enable data whitening to improve DC balance. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Current Gain
config_entries.description: Set this to the ratio of the differential voltage at the current inputs (in Volts) vs. the actual line current to be calculated (in Amperes). When using a shunt resistor as the current sensing element, this is going to simply equal the resistance since the differential voltage is the line current multiplied by the resistance. When using a current transformer, the value is going to be the burden resistor's value divided by the number of turns of the transformer winding. For a 2000 turn current transformer clamp and a 2 Ohm burden resistor this works out to 0.001 (the default if **current_gain** is not specified).

config_entries.label: Current Hpf
config_entries.description: Enables and disables the High-pass Filter on the current processing path in the CS5460A. Defaults to `true` (enabled).

config_entries.label: Pga Gain
config_entries.description: If set to `10X` (default), the differential voltage at the current inputs must be between -250mV and +250mV. If set to `50X` it must be within -100mV to +100mV.

config_entries.label: Phase Offset
config_entries.description: This can be used to account for a phase offset between the voltage sensing circuit and the current sensing circuit to improve power measurement accuracy. Admits integer values between -64 to 63, which should be offset by 0.5 and multiplied by about 8.2 CS5460A clock intervals to get the resulting time offset. With the typical 4.096 MHz clocking this scales to a range of -128 μs to 128 μs, or -2.3º to 2.3º phase offset at 50Hz and a -2.8º to 2.8º phase offset at 60Hz. Defaults to `0` (i.e. time offset of 4.1 MCLK cycles). An easy way to find the correct value is to plug in a resisitve load such as an incandescent light-bulb and find the `phase_offset` value that results in the highest power reported by the sensor.

config_entries.label: Pulse Energy
config_entries.description: Sets the energy (in Watt-hours) per individual pulse on the CS5460A's EOUT pin that can be used to driver external counters / meters or a LED. The allowed range depends on the gain parameters, defaults to `10 Wh`.

config_entries.label: Samples
config_entries.description: The number of samples that go into each reading -- determines that update interval of the sensors and the accuracy of the readings. This is the number N from the CS5460A datasheet, defined as the number of *conversion cycles* within a *computation cycle*. The component reports data at the end of each *computation cycle*. With the standard 4.096MHz clock rate, each *conversion* takes 0.25ms so setting this to 2000 means 0.5s update interval, 40000 means 10s update interval and so on, similarly for other clock-rates. It is recommended that the interval be an integer number of the mains AC cycles, so for the 50 Hz AC frequency countries the interval should be a multiple of 20ms, for the 60 Hz countries a multiple of 16.66 ms. Defaults to `4000` (1 second at 4.096MHz). Admits values from 1 to 16777215.

components.name: CT Clamp Current Sensor
components.description: The Current Transformer Clamp (`ct_clamp`  ) sensor allows you to hook up a CT Clamp to an analog voltage sensor (like the [ADC sensor](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/adc/)) and convert the readings to measured single phase AC current.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the sensor. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default device class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to check the sensor. Defaults to `60s`. The **update_interval** for `ct_clamp` has to be greater than **sample_duration**.

config_entries.label: Sensor
config_entries.description: The source sensor to measure voltage values from.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Sample Duration
config_entries.description: The time duration to sample the current clamp with. Higher values can increase accuracy. Defaults to `200ms` which would be 10 whole cycles on a 50Hz system.

config_entries.label: State Class
config_entries.description: The state class for the sensor. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default state class of a sensor.

components.name: Current Based Cover
components.description: The `current_based` cover platform allows you to create covers with position control by using current sensors to detect the fully-open and fully-closed states. This is pretty useful when using motors with integrated mechanical endstops. During cover operation, the component monitors the current consumption to detect when the motor has stopped.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the cover. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the cover in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cover/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cover/#device-class) for a list of available options.

config_entries.label: Close Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to be closed.

config_entries.label: Close Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time it takes the cover to close from the fully-open state.

config_entries.label: Close Moving Current Threshold
config_entries.description: The amount of current in Amps the motor should drain to consider the cover is closing.

config_entries.label: Close Sensor
config_entries.description: The close current sensor.

config_entries.label: Open Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to be opened.

config_entries.label: Open Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time it takes the cover to open up from the fully-closed state.

config_entries.label: Open Moving Current Threshold
config_entries.description: The amount of current in Amps the motor should drain to consider the cover is opening.

config_entries.label: Open Sensor
config_entries.description: The open current sensor.

config_entries.label: Stop Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed to stop the cover.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Close Obstacle Current Threshold
config_entries.description: The amount of current in Amps the motor should drain to consider the cover is blocked during closing.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Malfunction Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when relay malfunction is detected. Malfunction may require device servicing. You can use this action to notify other systems about this situation

config_entries.label: Malfunction Detection
config_entries.description: Enable to detect malfunction detection (Typically welded relays). Defaults to `True`.

config_entries.label: Max Duration
config_entries.description: The maximum duration the cover should be opening or closing. Useful for protecting from dysfunctional motor integrated endstops.

config_entries.label: Mqtt Json State Payload
config_entries.description: When set to `true`, state changes will be published only to the `state_topic` as a single JSON object per state change. Example: ```json { "state": "open", "position": 100, "tilt": 50 } ``` When `false`, individual values are published to the `state_topic`, `position_state_topic`, and `tilt_state_topic` separately. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Obstacle Rollback
config_entries.description: The percentage of rollback the cover will perform in case of obstacle detection. Defaults to `10%`.

config_entries.label: Open Obstacle Current Threshold
config_entries.description: The amount of current in Amps the motor should drain to consider the cover is blocked during opening.

config_entries.label: Position Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive cover position commands on.

config_entries.label: Position State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish cover position changes to. Not valid if `mqtt_json_state_payload` is set to `true`.

config_entries.label: Start Sensing Delay
config_entries.description: The amount of time the current sensing will be disabled when the movement starts. Motors can take some time before reaching their average consumption. Low values can cause an immediate stop because of the first current reading happening in the current-rising period. Defaults to `500ms`.

config_entries.label: Tilt Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive cover tilt commands on.

config_entries.label: Tilt State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish cover cover tilt state changes to. Not valid if `mqtt_json_state_payload` is set to `true`.

components.name: Debug Component
components.description: The `debug` component can be used to debug problems with ESPHome. At startup, it prints a bunch of useful information like reset reason, free heap size, ESPHome version and so on. It also allows you to get the same information as a text sensor, and to monitor the state of the ESP heap memory (free space, maximum free block size and fragmentation level) and the main-loop timing. Monitoring can be done via the logger or web server component if it has been configured.

components.name: Deep Sleep Component
components.description: The `deep_sleep` component can be used to automatically enter a deep sleep mode on the ESP8266/ESP32/BK72xx after a certain amount of time. This is especially useful with nodes that operate on batteries and therefore need to conserve as much energy as possible.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Esp32 Ext1 Wakeup
config_entries.description: Use the EXT1 wakeup source of the ESP32 to wake from deep sleep to wake up on multiple pins. This cannot be used together with wakeup pin.

config_entries.label: Mode
config_entries.description: The mode to use for the wakeup source. Must be one of:

options.label: wake up when all selected pins are LOW (ESP32 only)
wake up when any selected pin is HIGH
wake up when any selected pin is LOW (ESP32‑C5/C6/C61/H2/P4/S2/S3 only)

config_entries.label: Pins
config_entries.description: The pins to wake up on.

config_entries.label: Run Duration
config_entries.description: The time duration the node should be active, i.e. run code. Only on ESP32, instead of time, it is possible to specify run duration according to the wakeup reason from deep-sleep:

config_entries.label: Default
config_entries.description: default run duration for timer wakeup and any unspecified wakeup reason.

config_entries.label: Gpio Wakeup Reason
config_entries.description: run duration if woken up by GPIO.

config_entries.label: Touch Wakeup Reason
config_entries.description: run duration if woken up by touch.

config_entries.label: Sleep Duration
config_entries.description: The time duration to stay in deep sleep mode. On BK72xx, the maximum is 36 hours.

config_entries.label: Touch Wakeup
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. Use a touch event to wakeup from deep sleep. To be able to wakeup from a touch event, [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/esp32_touch#esp32-touch-binary-sensor) must be configured properly.

config_entries.label: Wakeup Pin
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32/BK72xx. A single pin to wake up to once in deep sleep mode. Use the inverted property to wake up to LOW signals. If you want to specify multiple wake-up pins (BK72xx only) specify them under `wakeup_pin` using a list of entries consisting of:

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals

While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.description: The state class for the sensor. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes) for a list of available options. config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the sensor. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default device class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default

config_entries.label: Entity Category

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

components.name: OpenEnergyMonitor EmonTx Sensors
components.description: The `emontx` component allows you to use ESPHome to create a connection to an OpenEnergyMonitor emonTX via a supported device (ESP32 recommended). This component is a global hub that establishes the connection to the EmonTx via [UART bus](https://esphome.io/components/uart) and translates the received data. Using the [emontx sensors](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/emontx#emontx-sensors), you can then create sensors for Home Assistant that track voltage, current, power as measured by CTs (up to 12), pulse data, and temperature depending on the configuration of the emonTX.

config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID of the [UART Component](https://esphome.io/components/uart) if you want to use multiple UART buses.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation or multiple hubs.

components.description: The `emontx` component allows you to use ESPHome to create a connection to an OpenEnergyMonitor emonTX via a supported device (ESP32 recommended). This component is a global hub that establishes the connection to the EmonTx via [UART bus](https://esphome.io/components/uart) and translates the received data. Using the [emontx sensors](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/emontx#emontx-sensors), you can then create sensors for Home Assistant that track voltage, current, power as measured by CTs (up to 12), pulse data, and temperature depending on the configuration of the emonTX.

components.name: Endstop Cover
components.description: The `endstop` cover platform allows you to create covers with position control that have endstops at both ends of the cover to detect the fully-open and fully-closed states. When any of these endstops are reached, the cover is stopped (via `stop_action`  ) and the corresponding state is sent out.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the cover. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the cover in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cover/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cover/#device-class) for a list of available options.

config_entries.label: Close Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to be closed.

config_entries.label: Close Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time it takes the cover to close from the fully-open state.

config_entries.label: Close Endstop
config_entries.description: The ID of the [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#config-binary_sensor) that turns on when the closed position is reached.

config_entries.label: Open Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to be opened.

config_entries.label: Open Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time it takes the cover to open up from the fully-closed state.

config_entries.label: Open Endstop
config_entries.description: The ID of the [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#config-binary_sensor) that turns on when the open position is reached.

config_entries.label: Stop Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to stop or an endstop is reached.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Max Duration
config_entries.description: The maximum duration the cover should be opening or closing. Useful for protecting from dysfunctional endstops.

config_entries.label: Mqtt Json State Payload
config_entries.description: When set to `true`, state changes will be published only to the `state_topic` as a single JSON object per state change. Example: ```json { "state": "open", "position": 100, "tilt": 50 } ``` When `false`, individual values are published to the `state_topic`, `position_state_topic`, and `tilt_state_topic` separately. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Position Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive cover position commands on.

config_entries.label: Position State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish cover position changes to. Not valid if `mqtt_json_state_payload` is set to `true`.

config_entries.label: Tilt Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive cover tilt commands on.

config_entries.label: Tilt State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish cover cover tilt state changes to. Not valid if `mqtt_json_state_payload` is set to `true`.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: Id

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Expire After

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

components.name: ESP32 Platform
components.description: This component contains platform-specific options for the ESP32 platform.

config_entries.label: Framework
config_entries.description: Options for the underlying framework used by ESPHome. See [Framework](https://esphome.io/components/esp32#esp32-framework).

config_entries.label: Variant
config_entries.description: The ESP32 mcu/chip to use for this device configuration. One of `esp32`, `esp32s2`, `esp32s3`, `esp32c2`, `esp32c3`, `esp32c5`, `esp32c6`, `esp32c61`, `esp32h2` or `esp32p4`. This must match the hardware in use, or it will fail to flash.

config_entries.label: Cpu Frequency
config_entries.description: The CPU frequency to use. Defaults to the maximum supported frequency for the variant. The allowed values depend on the variant:

config_entries.label: Engineering Sample
config_entries.description: **ESP32-P4 only.** Set to `true` if your board has engineering sample silicon (rev < 3.0). When using `variant: esp32p4` without specifying a `board`, a warning is logged if this option is not explicitly set. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Flash Size
config_entries.description: The amount of flash memory available on the ESP32 board/module. One of `2MB`, `4MB`, `8MB`, `16MB` or `32MB`. Defaults to `4MB`. **Warning: specifying a size larger than that available on your board will cause the ESP32 to fail to boot.**

config_entries.label: Partitions
config_entries.description: A partition table CSV file or a list of custom partitions to add. See [Partitions](https://esphome.io/components/esp32#esp32-partitions).

components.name: BLE Component
components.description: The `esp32_ble` component in ESPHome sets up the Bluetooth LE stack on the device so that a [Esp32 Ble Server](https://esphome.io/components/esp32_ble_server/) can run.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the BLE device.

config_entries.label: Advertising
config_entries.description: Manually enable BLE advertising support. This is automatically enabled when using [Esp32 Ble Server](https://esphome.io/components/esp32_ble_server/) or [Esp32 Ble Beacon](https://esphome.io/components/esp32_ble_beacon/). Only set this to `true` if you need advertising functionality without those components. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Advertising Cycle Time
config_entries.description: The time interval for cycling through multiple advertisements. Only applicable when advertising is enabled. Defaults to `10s`.

config_entries.label: Auth Req Mode
config_entries.description: The authentication request mode. Defaults to the ESP-IDF default. Leave unspecified unless your device needs special handling.

options.label: Secure connections with MITM and bonding

config_entries.label: Connection Timeout
config_entries.description: The maximum time to wait for a BLE connection to be established. Defaults to `20s`.

config_entries.label: Disable Bt Logs
config_entries.description: When enabled, disables Bluetooth logging categories that are not used by the configured components. This saves flash memory by only including the loggers needed by your configuration. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot
config_entries.description: If enabled, the BLE interface will be enabled on boot. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Io Capability
config_entries.description: The IO capability of this ESP32, used for securely connecting to other BLE devices. Defaults to `none`.

options.label: Only a display to show PIN codes
A display to show PIN codes and buttons to confirm or deny the connection
Only a keyboard to enter PIN codes (or a fixed PIN code)
No IO capability (Connections that require PIN code authentication will fail)

config_entries.label: Max Connections
config_entries.description: The maximum number of simultaneous BLE connections (client + server combined). Defaults to `3`.

config_entries.label: Max Key Size
config_entries.description: Maximum encryption key size to support. Must be between `7` and `16`. Leave unspecified to use the ESP32 default unless your device needs special handling.

config_entries.label: Max Notifications
config_entries.description: The maximum number of BLE characteristics that can have notifications enabled across all connections. Defaults to `12`.

config_entries.label: Min Key Size
config_entries.description: Minimum encryption key size requirement from peer. Must be between `7` and `16`. Leave unspecified to use the ESP32 default unless your device needs special handling.

components.name: ESP32 Bluetooth Low Energy Beacon
components.description: The `esp32_ble_beacon` component creates a Bluetooth Low Energy Beacon with your ESP32 device. Beacons are BLE devices that repeatedly just send out a pre-defined packet of data. This packet can then be received by devices like smartphones and can then be used to track a phone's location.

config_entries.label: Type
config_entries.description: The type of beacon to create, currently only supports `iBeacon`.

config_entries.label: Uuid
config_entries.description: The [universally unique identifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universally_unique_identifier) to identify the beacon.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation.

config_entries.label: Major
config_entries.description: The iBeacon major identifier of this beacon. Usually used to group beacons, for example for grouping all beacons in the same building, but has no effect if the BLE receiver doesn't use it. Defaults to `10167`.

config_entries.label: Max Interval
config_entries.description: The iBeacon maximum transmit interval in milliseconds from 20 to 10240. Setting this greater than `min_interval` gives the BLE hardware a better chance to avoid collisions with other BLE transmissions. Defaults to the iBeacon specification's defined interval: `100ms`.

config_entries.label: Measured Power
config_entries.description: The RSSI of the iBeacon as measured 1 meter from the device. This is used to calibrate the ranging calculations in iOS. The procedure for setting this value can be found in Apple's [Getting Started with iBeacon PDF](https://developer.apple.com/ibeacon/Getting-Started-with-iBeacon.pdf) under the heading *Calibrating iBeacon*. Between -128 to 0. Defaults to `-59`.

config_entries.label: Min Interval
config_entries.description: The iBeacon minimum transmit interval in milliseconds from 20 to 10240. Setting this less than `max_interval` gives the BLE hardware a better chance to avoid collisions with other BLE transmissions. Defaults to the iBeacon specification's defined interval: `100ms`.

config_entries.label: Minor
config_entries.description: The iBeacon minor identifier of this beacon. Usually used to identify beacons within an iBeacon group. Defaults to `61958`.

config_entries.label: Tx Power
config_entries.description: The transmit power of the iBeacon in dBm. One of -12, -9, -6, -3, 0, 3, 6, 9. Defaults to `3dBm`. Not available on ESP-Hosted platforms (e.g., ESP32-P4).

components.name: BLE Server
components.description: The `esp32_ble_server` component in ESPHome sets up a BLE GATT server that exposes the device name, manufacturer and board. BLE GATT services and characteristics can be added to the server to expose data and control.

config_entries.label: Model
config_entries.description: The model name of the device. Defaults to the project's name defined in the [core configuration](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-creators_project) if present, otherwise to the friendly name of the `board` chosen in the [core configuration](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-configuration_variables).

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The ID of the descriptor to set the value of.

config_entries.label: Appearance
config_entries.description: Sets the [appearance](https://bitbucket.org/bluetooth-SIG/public/src/main/assigned_numbers/core/appearance_values.yaml) of the device (included in advertising data.) Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Firmware Version
config_entries.description: The firmware version of the device. Defaults to the project's version defined in the [core configuration](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-creators_project) if present, otherwise to the ESPHome version.

config_entries.label: Manufacturer
config_entries.description: The name of the manufacturer/firmware creator. Defaults to `ESPHome`.

config_entries.label: Manufacturer Data
config_entries.description: The manufacturer-specific data to include in the advertising packet. Should be a list of bytes, where the first two are the little-endian representation of the 16-bit manufacturer ID as assigned by the Bluetooth SIG.

config_entries.label: Max Clients
config_entries.description: The maximum number of simultaneous BLE client connections the server will accept. When set to a value greater than 1, the server resumes advertising after a client connects so that additional clients can discover and connect, up to this limit. Must not exceed the `max_connections` value configured in the [ESP32 BLE](https://esphome.io/components/esp32_ble) component. Defaults to `1`. Range: 1 to 9.

config_entries.label: Services
config_entries.description: A list of services to expose on the BLE GATT server.

components.name: ESP32 Bluetooth Low Energy Tracker Hub
components.description: The `esp32_ble_tracker` component creates a global hub so that you can track bluetooth low energy devices using your ESP32 node.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for this ESP32 BLE Hub.

config_entries.label: Max Connections
config_entries.description: **DEPRECATED** - This option has been moved to the [Esp32 Ble](https://esphome.io/components/esp32_ble/) component. Please configure `max_connections` there instead. This option is kept for backward compatibility only. This option will be removed in ESPHome 2026.10.0.

config_entries.label: Scan Parameters
config_entries.description: Advanced parameters for configuring the scan behavior of the ESP32. See also [this guide by Texas Instruments](https://dev.ti.com/tirex/explore/content/simplelink_academy_cc2640r2sdk_5_10_02_00/modules/blestack/ble_scan_adv_basic/ble_scan_adv_basic.html#scanning-basics) for reference.

config_entries.label: Active
config_entries.description: Whether to actively send scan requests to request more data after having received an advertising packet. With some devices this is necessary to receive all data, but also drains those devices' power a bit more. Some devices don't need this, in that case you can save power and RF pollution by setting it to `false`. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Continuous
config_entries.description: Whether to scan continuously (forever) or to only scan when asked to start a scan (with start_scan action). Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Duration
config_entries.description: The duration of each complete scan. This has no real impact on the device but can be used to debug the BLE stack. Defaults to `5min`.

config_entries.label: Interval
config_entries.description: The interval between each consecutive scan window. This is the time the ESP spends on each of the 3 BLE advertising channels. Defaults to `320ms`.

config_entries.label: Window
config_entries.description: The time the ESP is actively listening for packets on a channel during each scan interval. If this is close to the `interval` value, the ESP will spend more time listening to packets (but also consume more power). Defaults to `30ms`

config_entries.label: Software Coexistence
config_entries.description: When enabled, software coexistence will briefly prioritize Bluetooth over Wi-Fi during the initial establishment of BLE connections, which can improve reliability. Only available if `wifi` component is configured. Defaults to `true`.

components.name: ESP32 Camera Component
components.description: The `esp32_camera` component allows you to use ESP32-based camera boards in ESPHome that directly integrate into Home Assistant through the native API.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the camera.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the camera in the frontend.

config_entries.label: I2C Id
config_entries.description: The ID of the [I²C bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) the camera is connected to.

config_entries.label: Data Pins
config_entries.description: The data lanes of the camera, this must be a list of 8 GPIO pins.

config_entries.label: External Clock
config_entries.description: The configuration of the external clock to drive the camera.

config_entries.label: Pin

config_entries.label: Frequency

config_entries.label: Href Pin
config_entries.description: The pin the HREF line of the camera is connected to.

config_entries.label: Pixel Clock Pin
config_entries.description: The pin the pixel clock line of the camera is connected to.

config_entries.label: Power Down Pin
config_entries.description: The ESP pin to power down the camera. If set, this will power down the camera while it is inactive.

config_entries.label: Reset Pin
config_entries.description: The ESP pin the reset pin of the camera is connected to. If set, this will reset the camera before the ESP boots.

config_entries.label: Vsync Pin
config_entries.description: The pin the VSYNC line of the camera is connected to.

config_entries.label: Ae Level
config_entries.description: The auto exposure level to apply to the picture (when **aec_mode** is set to `auto`  ), from -2 to 2. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Aec2
config_entries.description: Whether to enable Auto Exposure Control 2. Seems to change computation method of automatic exposure. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Aec Mode
config_entries.description: The mode of exposure module. Defaults to `auto` (leave camera to automatically adjust exposure).

config_entries.label: Aec Value
config_entries.description: The Exposure value to apply to the picture (when **aec_mode** is set to `manual`  ), from 0 to 1200. Defaults to `300`.

config_entries.label: Agc Gain Ceiling
config_entries.description: The maximum gain allowed, when **agc_mode** is set to `auto`. This parameter seems act as "ISO" setting. Defaults to `2x`.

config_entries.label: Agc Mode
config_entries.description: The mode of gain control module. Defaults to `auto` (leave camera to automatically adjust sensor gain).

config_entries.label: Agc Value
config_entries.description: The gain value to apply to the picture (when **aec_mode** is set to `manual`  ), from 0 to 30. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Brightness
config_entries.description: The brightness to apply to the picture, from -2 to 2. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Contrast
config_entries.description: The contrast to apply to the picture, from -2 to 2. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Frame Buffer Count
config_entries.description: The number of frame buffers to use when reading from the camera sensor. Must be between 1 and 2. Defaults to `1`.

config_entries.label: Frame Buffer Location
config_entries.description: The memory area used for storing the frame buffers. Defaults to `PSRAM`.

config_entries.label: Horizontal Mirror
config_entries.description: Whether to mirror the image horizontally. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Idle Framerate
config_entries.description: The framerate to capture images at when no client is requesting a full stream. Defaults to `0.1 fps`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Jpeg Quality
config_entries.description: The JPEG quality that the camera should encode images with. From 6 (best) to 63 (worst). Defaults to `10`. Set this to ``0`` to disable JPEG compression/conversion. Manual JPEG compression/conversion requires `psram` component to be enabled and configured.

config_entries.label: Max Framerate
config_entries.description: The maximum framerate the camera will generate images at. Up to 60Hz is possible (with reduced frame sizes), but beware of overheating. Defaults to `10 fps`.

config_entries.label: Pixel Format
config_entries.description: The pixel format to use for the images. Defaults to ``jpeg`` (JPEG compressed image) which may not be supported by all cameras. Other formats require more CPU and memory and may not be supported by all cameras.

config_entries.label: Resolution
config_entries.description: The resolution the camera will capture images at. Higher resolutions require more memory, if there's not enough memory you will see an error during startup.

config_entries.label: Saturation
config_entries.description: The saturation to apply to the picture, from -2 to 2. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Special Effect
config_entries.description: The effect to apply to the picture. Defaults to `none` (picture without effect).

config_entries.label: Test Pattern
config_entries.description: For tests purposes, it's possible to replace picture get from sensor by a test color pattern. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Vertical Flip
config_entries.description: Whether to flip the image vertically. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Wb Mode
config_entries.description: The mode of white balace module. Defaults to `auto`.

components.name: ESP32 Camera Web Server Component
