config_entries.label: Mode
config_entries.description: The operation mode. One of these values:

config_entries.label: Port
config_entries.description: The serving port.

components.name: ESP32 CAN
components.description: The ESP32 has an integrated CAN controller and therefore doesn't necessarily need an external controller. Some variants (ESP32-C5, ESP32-C6, ESP32-P4) have multiple CAN controllers - see [Multiple CAN Controllers](https://esphome.io/components/canbus/esp32_can#multiple-can-controllers) below. You only need to specify the RX and TX pins. Any GPIO will work.

config_entries.label: Rx Pin
config_entries.description: Receive pin.

config_entries.label: Tx Pin
config_entries.description: Transmit pin.

config_entries.label: Mode
config_entries.description: Operating mode. One of:

options.label: Receive data only, no ACK signals sent.

config_entries.label: Rx Queue Len
config_entries.description: Length of RX queue.

config_entries.label: Tx Enqueue Timeout
config_entries.description: Maximum time to wait when the TX queue is full before dropping the message (by default, this is set to the time it takes to send 10 CAN messages at the given bit rate).

config_entries.label: Tx Queue Len
config_entries.description: Length of TX queue, 0 to disable.

components.name: ESP32 DAC
components.description: The ESP32 DAC platform allows you to output analog voltages using the 8-bit digital-to-analog converter of the ESP32. Unlike the [Ledc](https://esphome.io/components/output/ledc/), which can simulate an analog signal by using a fast switching frequency, the hardware DAC can output a *real* analog signal with no need for additional filtering.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The pin to use DAC on. See above for valid pin numbers.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The id to use for this output component.

components.name: ESP32 Hosted
components.description: ESP32 Hosted ([ESP-Hosted-MCU](https://github.com/espressif/esp-hosted-mcu)) is a solution that allows you to use ESP32 modules as communication co-processors. This solution provides wireless connectivity (Wi-Fi and Bluetooth) to the host module, enabling it to communicate with other devices.

components.name: ESP32 Hosted Co-processor Update
components.description: ESP32 Hosted update platform to manage co-processor firmware updates.

components.name: Improv via BLE
components.description: The `esp32_improv` component in ESPHome implements the open [Improv standard](https://www.improv-wifi.com/) for configuring Wi-Fi on an ESP32 device by using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) to receive the credentials.

config_entries.label: Authorizer
config_entries.description: A [binary sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor/) to authorize with. Also accepts `none` to skip authorization.

config_entries.label: Status Indicator
config_entries.description: An [output](https://esphome.io/components/output/) to display feedback to the user.

config_entries.label: Authorized Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time until authorization times out and needs to be re-authorized. Defaults to `1min`.

config_entries.label: Identify Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time to identify for. Defaults to `10s`.

config_entries.label: Next Url
config_entries.description: The URL to open after provisioning is complete. Defaults to `https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/config_flow_start?domain=esphome`.

config_entries.label: Wifi Timeout
config_entries.description: The amount of time to wait before starting the Improv service after Wi-Fi is no longer connected. Defaults to `90s`.

components.name: ESP32 RMT LED Strip
components.description: This is a component using the ESP32 RMT peripheral to drive most addressable LED strips.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the light. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the light in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The pin for the data line of the light.

config_entries.label: Restore Mode
config_entries.description: Control how the light attempts to restore state on bootup.

options.label: Always initialize the light as ON on bootup.
Attempt to restore state but initialize the light as OFF.
Attempt to restore state but initialize the light as ON.
Attempt to restore state and default to OFF if not possible to restore.
Attempt to restore state and default to ON.
Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to OFF.
Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to ON.

config_entries.label: Num Leds
config_entries.description: The number of LEDs in the strip.

config_entries.label: Rgb Order
config_entries.description: The RGB order of the strip.

config_entries.label: Bit0 High
config_entries.description: The time to hold the data line high for a `0` bit.

config_entries.label: Bit0 Low
config_entries.description: The time to hold the data line low for a `0` bit.

config_entries.label: Bit1 High
config_entries.description: The time to hold the data line high for a `1` bit.

config_entries.label: Bit1 Low
config_entries.description: The time to hold the data line low for a `1` bit.

config_entries.label: Blue
config_entries.description: The blue channel of the light.

config_entries.label: Brightness
config_entries.description: The primary brightness of the light; applies to all channels (both color and white) of the light.

config_entries.label: Chipset
config_entries.description: The name of the chipset used; determines signal timing. Not required if [specifying the timings manually](https://esphome.io/components/light/esp32_rmt_led_strip#esp32-rmt-led-strip-manual_timings).

config_entries.label: Cold White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the cold white channel. Cannot be used at the same time as *color_temperature*.

config_entries.label: Color Temperature
config_entries.description: The color temperature (in [mireds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mired) or Kelvin) of the white channel.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Effects
config_entries.description: A list of [light effects](https://esphome.io/components/light#light-effects) to use for this light.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [this list](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Green
config_entries.description: The green channel of the light.

config_entries.label: Initial State
config_entries.description: The initial state the light should be set to on bootup. This state will be applied when the state is **not** restored based on `restore_mode` (below).

config_entries.label: State
config_entries.description: The ON/OFF state for the light.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Is Rgbw
config_entries.description: Set to `true` if the strip is RGBW. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Is Wrgb
config_entries.description: Set to `true` if the strip is WRGB. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Max Refresh Rate
config_entries.description: A time interval used to limit the number of commands a light can handle per second. For example, `16ms` will limit the light to a refresh rate of about 60Hz. Defaults to sending commands as quickly as changes are made to the lights.

config_entries.label: Red
config_entries.description: The red channel of the light.

config_entries.label: Reset High
config_entries.description: The time to hold the data line high after writing the state. Defaults to `0 us`.

config_entries.label: Reset Low
config_entries.description: The time to hold the data line low after writing the state. Defaults to `0 us`.

config_entries.label: Rmt Symbols
config_entries.description: When `use_dma` is enabled, this sets the size of the driver's internal DMA buffer. When DMA is disabled, it specifies how much RMT memory is allocated to the component. RMT memory is shared across all components and should be allocated in multiples of the block size. On the `ESP32` and `ESP32-S2` variants, RMT memory is shared between RX and TX components. On other variants, RX and TX have dedicated RMT memory.

config_entries.label: Use Dma
config_entries.description: Enable DMA on variants that support it. If enabled `rmt_symbols` controls the DMA buffer size and can be set to a large value.

config_entries.label: Use Psram
config_entries.description: Set to `false` to force internal RAM allocation even if you have the PSRAM component enabled. This can be useful if you're experiencing issues like flickering with your leds strip. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Warm White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the warm white channel. Cannot be used at the same time as *color_temperature*.

config_entries.label: White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the white channel.

components.name: ESP32 Touch Pad
components.description: Capacitive touch detection is possible on ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3 and ESP32-P4 processors. In ESPHome, it is configured in two parts:

config_entries.label: Waterproof Guard Ring
config_entries.description: Sets the touch channel to use for the guard pad. The guard pad is used to detect the large area of water covering the touch panel.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation.

config_entries.label: Debounce Count
config_entries.description: Sets the debounce count; if the measured values continue to exceed the threshold for `n + 1` times, the touch sensor state changes.

config_entries.label: Denoise Cap Level
config_entries.description: Select internal reference capacitance of denoise channel. Must be one of `L0`, `L1`, `L2`, `L3`, `L4`, `L5`, `L6` or `L7`.

config_entries.label: Denoise Grade
config_entries.description: Sets the denoise range of the denoise channel. Determined by measuring the noise amplitude of the denoise channel. Must be one of `BIT12`, `BIT10`, `BIT8` or `BIT4`.

config_entries.label: Filter Mode
config_entries.description: Sets the filter mode. Must be one of `IIR_4`, `IIR_8`, `IIR_16`, `IIR_32`, `IIR_64`, `IIR_128`, `IIR_256` (S2/S3 only) or `JITTER`.

config_entries.label: High Voltage Reference
config_entries.description: The high voltage reference to use for the charge cycles. One of `2.4V`, `2.5V`, `2.6V`, `2.7V`. Default is `2.7V`.

config_entries.label: Iir Filter
config_entries.description: Optionally set up an [Infinite Impulse Response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinite_impulse_response) filter should be applied to all touch pads. This can increase the accuracy of the touch pads a lot, but higher values decrease the response time. A good value to start with is `10ms`. By default, the IIR filter is inactive.

config_entries.label: Jitter Step
config_entries.description: Set jitter filter step size.

config_entries.label: Low Voltage Reference
config_entries.description: The low voltage reference to use for the charge cycles. One of `0.5V`, `0.6V`, `0.7V`, `0.8V`. Default is `0.5V`.

config_entries.label: Measurement Duration
config_entries.description: Set the conversion time for all touch pads. A longer conversion time means that more charge/discharge cycles of the touch pad can be performed, therefore increasing accuracy. Default is about 8ms, the maximum amount.

config_entries.label: Noise Threshold
config_entries.description: Noise threshold coefficient. Higher = More noise resistance. The actual noise should be less than (noise coefficient * touch threshold). The coefficient is 0: 4/8; 1: 3/8; 2: 2/8; 3: 1.

config_entries.label: Setup Mode
config_entries.description: Whether debug messages with the touch pad value should

config_entries.label: Sleep Duration
config_entries.description: Set a time period denoting the amount of time the touch peripheral should sleep between measurements. This can decrease power usage but make the sensor slower. Default is about 27 milliseconds.

config_entries.label: Smooth Mode
config_entries.description: Level of filter applied on the original data against large noise interference. Must be one of `OFF`, `IIR_2`, `IIR_4` or `IIR_8`.

config_entries.label: Voltage Attenuation
config_entries.description: The voltage attenuation to use for the charge cycles. One of `1.5V`, `1V`, `0.5V`, `0V`. Default is `0V`.

config_entries.label: Waterproof Shield Driver
config_entries.description: Shield channel drive capability configuration; the larger the parasitic capacitance on the shielding channel, the higher the drive capability needs to be set. Must be one of `L0`, `L1`, `L2`, `L3`, `L4`, `L5`, `L6` or `L7`.

components.name: ESP32 Touch Pad
components.description: The `esp32_touch` binary sensor platform lets you use the touch peripheral of the ESP32 to detect if a certain pin is being "touched".

config_entries.description: The name for the binary sensor. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the binary sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The pin to detect touch

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/binary_sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/binary_sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options.

config_entries.label: Threshold
config_entries.description: The threshold to use to detect touch events. See

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: A list of filters to apply on the binary sensor values such as inverting signals. See [Binary Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#binary_sensor-filters).

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Trigger On Initial State
config_entries.description: If true, any applicable triggers will be fired when the binary sensor state changes from `unknown` to a valid state. This applies to the first valid state set, and any valid state set after a `binary_sensor.invalidate_state` action has been executed. The default is `false`.

config_entries.label: Wakeup Threshold
config_entries.description: The threshold to use to detect touch events to wake-up from deep sleep.

components.name: ESP8266 Platform
components.description: This component contains platform-specific options for the ESP8266 platform.

config_entries.label: Framework
config_entries.description: Options for the underlying framework used by ESPHome.

config_entries.label: Platform Version
config_entries.description: The version of the [platformio/espressif8266](https://github.com/platformio/platform-espressif8266/releases/) package to use.

config_entries.label: Source
config_entries.description: The PlatformIO package or repository to use for the framework. This can be used to use a custom or patched version of the framework.

config_entries.label: Version
config_entries.description: The base framework version number to use, from [esp8266 arduino releases](https://github.com/esp8266/Arduino/releases). Defaults to `recommended`. Additional values

config_entries.label: Board Flash Mode
config_entries.description: The SPI mode of the flash chip. One of `qio`, `qout`, `dio` and `dout`. Defaults to `dout` for compatibility with all chips. Note: on the next OTA update the actual flash mode is automatically detected and changed to the appropriate one.

config_entries.label: Early Pin Init
config_entries.description: Specifies whether pins should be initialised as early as possible to known values. Recommended value is `false` where switches are involved, as these will toggle when updating the firmware or when restarting the device. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Enable Full Printf
config_entries.description: Enable full `FILE*`-based printf support. By default, ESPHome wraps `printf()`, `vprintf()`, and `fprintf()` with lightweight stubs that use `vsnprintf()` + `fwrite()`, saving ~1.6 KB of flash. ESPHome logging writes directly to the UART via Arduino's `Serial`, not libc printf, so these functions are typically unused unless an external component calls them. Set to `true` only if an external component needs full `FILE*`-based printf. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Enable Scanf Float
config_entries.description: Enable float support for `scanf()`/`sscanf()`. By default, ESPHome removes the `-u _scanf_float` linker flag to save ~8 KB of flash. This means `sscanf()` with `%f` will silently fail to parse floating-point numbers. Nothing in ESPHome itself uses scanf; set to `true` only if you use `sscanf()` with `%f` in lambdas. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Enable Serial
config_entries.description: Force-enable the Arduino `Serial` object (UART0) for use in lambdas or external libraries. Most users will never need this option, as the `logger` and `uart` components automatically enable the required Serial objects. Only use this if you directly access `Serial` in a lambda and get a compilation error. Use the [UART component](https://esphome.io/components/uart) instead when possible, as it works across all platforms. Defaults to automatic detection.

config_entries.label: Enable Serial1
config_entries.description: Force-enable the Arduino `Serial1` object (UART1) for use in lambdas or external libraries. Most users will never need this option, as the `logger` and `uart` components automatically enable the required Serial objects. Only use this if you directly access `Serial1` in a lambda and get a compilation error. Use the [UART component](https://esphome.io/components/uart) instead when possible, as it works across all platforms. Defaults to automatic detection.

config_entries.label: Restore From Flash
config_entries.description: Whether to store some persistent preferences in flash memory. Defaults to `false`.

components.name: ESP8266 Software PWM Output
components.description: The ESP8266 Software PWM platform allows you to use a software PWM on the pins GPIO0-GPIO16 on your ESP8266. Note that this is a software PWM, so there can be some flickering during periods of high WiFi activity. Hardware PWMs like the one on the ESP32 (see [Ledc](https://esphome.io/components/output/ledc/)) are preferred.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The pin to use PWM on.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The id to use for this output component.

config_entries.label: Frequency
config_entries.description: The frequency to run the PWM with. Lower frequencies have more visual artifacts, but can represent much more colors. Defaults to `1kHz`.

components.name: ESP32-P4 LDO
components.description: The ESP32-P4 has 4 Low-Dropout linear regulators that can be used to power on- and off-chip peripherals. This component allows those regulators to be configured and enabled.

config_entries.label: Channel
config_entries.description: The channel number of the LDO regulator to configure. Valid values are 1–4. Channels 3 and 4 are available for general use. Channels 1 and 2 are reserved for internal chip use (flash/PSRAM) and require ``allow_internal_channel: true`` to be set.

config_entries.label: Voltage
config_entries.description: The desired output voltage. Must be in the range ``0.5V`` to ``2.7V``, or ``passthrough`` to enable pass-through mode (output follows the supply voltage). Note: the actual output voltage may deviate by approximately 50–100 mV from the configured value.

config_entries.label: Adjustable
config_entries.description: If true, the output voltage can be adjusted at runtime using the ``esp_ldo.voltage.adjust`` action. Defaults to ``false``. Cannot be set to ``true`` when ``voltage`` is ``passthrough``, as pass-through mode does not support runtime voltage adjustment.

config_entries.label: Allow Internal Channel
config_entries.description: Must be set to ``true`` to use channels 1 or 2. These channels are normally reserved by the chip for flash and PSRAM power. Incorrect use can cause system instability, data corruption, or a permanently bricked device. Only set this if you have verified via your board's datasheet and schematics that the channel is unused. Setting this option on channels 3 or 4 is an error. Defaults to ``false``.

components.name: ESPHome Core Configuration
components.description: Here you specify some core information that ESPHome needs to create firmwares. Most importantly, this is the section of the configuration where you specify the **name** of the node.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: This is the name of the node. It should always be unique in your ESPHome network. May only contain lowercase characters, digits and hyphens, and can be at most 24 characters long by default, or 31 characters long if `name_add_mac_suffix` is `false`. See [Changing ESPHome Node Name](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-changing_node_name).

config_entries.label: Friendly Name
config_entries.description: This name is sent to the frontend and used by Home Assistant as the integration and device name. It also gets prefixed to entity names when needed. While optional, leaving it out can result in less intuitive names and a less polished experience in Home Assistant. Setting a `friendly_name` helps keep things clear, consistent, and easier to manage.

config_entries.label: Area
config_entries.description: The area configuration for this device. This is sent to Home Assistant to specify which area/zone the device belongs to. Can be either a simple string (e.g., `"Living Room"`  ) or a structured format with `id` and `name`.

config_entries.label: Areas
config_entries.description: Additional areas that can be referenced by devices.

config_entries.label: Comment
config_entries.description: Additional text information about this node. Only for display in UI.

config_entries.label: Build Path
config_entries.description: Customize where ESPHome will store the build files for your node. By default, ESPHome puts the PlatformIO project it uses to build the firmware in the `.esphome/build/<NODE>` (or into path from `ESPHOME_BUILD_PATH` environment variable if specified) directory, but you can customize this behavior using this option. Official docker image automatically use `/build` folder as default one in case it is mounted to it.

config_entries.label: Compile Process Limit
config_entries.description: The maximum number of simultaneous compile processes to run. Defaults to the number of cores of the CPU which is also the maximum you can set.

config_entries.label: Debug Scheduler
config_entries.description: If set, the scheduler will print debug information about scheduled tasks at log level DEBUG.

config_entries.label: Devices
config_entries.description: Sub-devices to group entities under.

config_entries.label: Environment Variables
config_entries.description: Environment variables to set during the build process. See [`environment_variables`](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-environment_variables).

config_entries.label: Includes
config_entries.description: A list of C/C++ files to include in the (auto-generated) `main` file. The paths in this list are relative to the directory where the YAML configuration file is located or `<...>` includes. See [`includes`](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-includes).

config_entries.label: Includes C
config_entries.description: The same as `includes` but for files that require C linkage. All includes will be wrapped in `extern "C" {}`. See [`includes`](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-includes).

config_entries.label: Libraries
config_entries.description: A list of libraries to include in the project. See [`libraries`](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-libraries).

config_entries.label: Min Version
config_entries.description: The minimum ESPHome version required to compile this configuration. See [Minimum ESPHome version](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-min_version).

config_entries.label: Name Add Mac Suffix
config_entries.description: Appends the last 3 bytes of the mac address of the device to the name in the form `<name>-aabbcc`. Defaults to `false`. See [Adding the MAC address as a suffix to the device name](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-mac_suffix).

config_entries.label: Platformio Options
config_entries.description: Additional options to pass over to PlatformIO in the platformio.ini file. See [`platformio_options`](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-platformio_options).

config_entries.label: Project
config_entries.description: ESPHome Creator's Project information. See [Project information](https://esphome.io/components/esphome#esphome-creators_project).

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: Name of the project

config_entries.label: Version
config_entries.description: Version of the project

components.name: ESPHome OTA Updates
components.description: ESPHome's Over-The-Air (OTA) platform to allow remote updating of devices.

config_entries.label: Password
config_entries.description: The password to use for updates.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Port
config_entries.description: The port to use for OTA updates. Defaults.

config_entries.label: Version
config_entries.description: Version of OTA protocol to use. Version 2 is more stable. To downgrade to legacy ESPHome, the device should be updated with OTA version 1 first. Defaults to 2.

components.name: ESPNow communication Component
components.description: The ESPNow component allows ESPHome to communicate with esp32 devices in a simple and unrestricted way. It enables the option to interact with other esp32 devices over the Espressif's ESP-NOW protocol, see [documentation](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/api-reference/network/esp_now.html). It can be used with the [Packet Transport Component](https://esphome.io/components/packet_transport) to broadcast sensor data, see [ESP-NOW Packet Transport Platform](https://esphome.io/components/packet_transport/espnow).

config_entries.label: Auto Add Peer
config_entries.description: This will allow the esp-now component to automatically add any new incoming device as a peer. See [Peers](https://esphome.io/components/espnow#espnow-peers) below. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Channel
config_entries.description: The Wi-Fi channel that the esp-now communication will use to send/receive data packets. Cannot be set when the [Wifi](https://esphome.io/components/wifi/) is used, as it will use the same channel as the wifi network.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot
config_entries.description: Enable the esp-now component on boot. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Peers
config_entries.description: A peer is the name for devices that use esp-now. The list will have all MAC addresses from the devices where this device may communicate with. See [Peers](https://esphome.io/components/espnow#espnow-peers) below.

components.name: ESP-NOW Packet Transport Platform
components.description: An ESP-NOW packet transport platform on ESPHome

config_entries.label: Ip Address

components.name: Feedback Cover
components.description: The `feedback` cover platform allows you to create covers with position control that can optionally have feedback from sensors to detect the fully-open and fully-closed states (endstops), and from sensors to detect actual movement (opening/closing). In all the cases the current position is approximated with the time the cover has been moving in a direction.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the cover. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.description: The interval to publish updated position information to the UI while the cover is moving. Defaults to `1s`.

config_entries.label: Close Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to be closed.

config_entries.label: Close Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time it takes the cover to close from the fully-open state.

config_entries.label: Close Endstop
config_entries.description: The ID of the [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#config-binary_sensor) that turns on when the closed position is reached.

config_entries.label: Close Obstacle Sensor
config_entries.description: The ID of the [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#config-binary_sensor) that turns on when an obstacle that blocks the close direction is detected.

config_entries.label: Open Endstop
config_entries.description: The ID of the [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#config-binary_sensor) that turns on when the open position is reached.

config_entries.description: The ID of the [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#config-binary_sensor) that turns on when an obstacle that blocks the open direction is detected.

config_entries.label: Open Sensor
config_entries.description: The ID of the [Binary Sensor](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#config-binary_sensor) that turns on when the cover is moving in the open direction.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Acceleration Wait Time
config_entries.description: Considers a wait time needed by the cover to actually start moving after command is issued and takes it into account when computing cover position (useful for heavy covers with large inertia). Intended to not accumulate error when doing multiple partial open/close actions). The open/close duration includes one instance of this delay, as it is the total amount of time from issuing a command to reaching endstop. Defaults to `0s`.

config_entries.label: Assumed State
config_entries.description: Whether the true state of the cover is not known. This will make the Home Assistant frontend show buttons for both OPEN and CLOSE actions, instead of hiding or disabling one of them. Defaults to `true` if no sensor is available to known the actual state of the cover.

config_entries.label: Direction Change Wait Time
config_entries.description: Stops cover and forces a wait time between changes in direction, and takes it into account when computing cover position (useful to protect motors). When this option is set (even at 0s) if an open/close action is invoked while the cover is moving in the opposite direction, then and intermediate stop action will be invoked to generate the delay.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default

config_entries.label: Mqtt Json State Payload

config_entries.label: Obstacle Rollback
config_entries.description: The percentage of rollback the cover will perform in case of obstacle detection while moving. Defaults to `10%`.

config_entries.label: Position Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive cover position commands on.

config_entries.label: Position State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish cover position changes to. Not valid if `mqtt_json_state_payload` is set to `true`.

config_entries.label: Tilt Command Topic

config_entries.label: Tilt State Topic

components.name: Font Renderer Component
components.description: ESPHome's graphical rendering engine also has a powerful font drawer which integrates seamlessly into the system. You have the option to use **any** OpenType/TrueType (`.ttf`, `.otf`, `.woff`  ) font file at **any** size, as well as fixed-size [PCF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portable_Compiled_Format) and [BDF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glyph_Bitmap_Distribution_Format) bitmap fonts.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The ID with which you will be able to reference the font later in your display code.

config_entries.label: File
config_entries.description: The path (relative to where the .yaml file is) of the font file. You can also use the `gfonts://` short form to use Google Fonts, or use the below structure:

config_entries.label: Bpp
config_entries.description: The bit depth of the rendered font from OpenType/TrueType, for anti-aliasing. Can be `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`. Defaults to `1`. If set to 1 and the font has a bitmap version available at the requested size, that will be used. Otherwise the font will be rendered from the vector representation.

config_entries.label: Extras
config_entries.description: A list of font glyph configurations you'd like to include within this font, from other OpenType/TrueType files (eg. icons from other font, but at the same size as the main font):

config_entries.label: File
config_entries.description: The path of the font file with the extra glyphs.

config_entries.label: Glyphs
config_entries.description: A list of glyphs you want to include. Can't repeat the same glyph codepoint if it was declared in the level above.

config_entries.label: Glyphs
config_entries.description: A list of characters you plan to use, in addition to the characters defined by the **glyphsets** option above. Adjust this list if you need some special characters or want to reduce the size of the binary if you don't plan to use certain glyphs. Both single characters (`a, b, c`  ) or strings of characters (`abc, def`  ) are acceptable options. You can also specify glyphs by their codepoint (see below).

config_entries.label: Glyphsets
config_entries.description: A list of glyphsets you plan to use. Defaults to `GF_Latin_Kernel`, which contains the basic characters and necessary punctuation and symbols for the English language. `GF_Latin_Core` is a more extended set that includes glyphs for the languages of Europe and the Americas with over 5 million speakers. Other options include `GF_Arabic_Core`, `GF_Cyrillic_Core`, `GF_Greek_Core`, their `Plus` variants, as well as `GF_Latin_African`, `GF_Latin_PriAfrican` and `GF_Latin_Vietnamese`. See the [Google Fonts Glyphset documentation](https://github.com/googlefonts/glyphsets/blob/main/GLYPHSETS.md) for an extensive list of all possible sets, along with their names and the languages supported by each of those sets. Note that `GF_Latin_Kernel` may need to be included for glyphs for basic characters such as numbers (0-9) and whitespace to be present.

config_entries.label: Ignore Missing Glyphs
config_entries.description: By default, warnings are generated for any glyph that is included in the defined **glyphsets** but not present in the configured font. Use this setting to suppress those warnings. Please note that the absence of any manually defined glyphs (specified via the **glyphs** option) will always be treated as an error and will not be influenced by this setting.

config_entries.label: Size
config_entries.description: The desired size of the font. This will be the size (height) of the font in pixels when rendered. If you want to use the same font in different sizes, create two font objects. Defaults to `20` for scalable fonts and the first available size for bitmap fonts. Requesting a size that is not available in a bitmap-only font will result in an error.

components.name: H-bridge Fan
components.description: The `hbridge` fan platform allows you to use a compatible *h-bridge* (L298N, DRV8871, MX1508, BTS7960, L9110S, DRV8833, TB6612, etc.) to control a fan (or motor/solenoid).

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the fan. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the fan in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Restore Mode
config_entries.description: Control how the fan attempts to restore state on boot.

options.label: Always initialize the fan as ON on bootup.
Attempt to restore state and default to OFF if not possible to restore.
Attempt to restore state and default to ON.
Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to OFF.
Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to ON.

config_entries.description: The id of the [float output](https://esphome.io/components/output/) connected to the Enable pin of the h-bridge (if h-bridge uses enable).

config_entries.label: Pin A
config_entries.description: The id of the [float output](https://esphome.io/components/output/) connected to Pin A (alternatively IN1, etc.) of the h-bridge.

config_entries.label: Pin B
config_entries.description: The id of the [float output](https://esphome.io/components/output/) connected to Pin B (alternatively IN2, etc.) of the h-bridge.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Decay Mode
config_entries.description: The decay mode you want to use with the h-bridge. Either `slow` (coasting) or `fast` (braking). Defaults to `slow`.

config_entries.label: Direction Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive fan direction commands on (options: forward, reverse, toggle).

config_entries.label: Direction State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish fan direction state changes to (options: forward, reverse).

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Oscillation Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive oscillation commands on.

config_entries.label: Oscillation State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish fan oscillation state changes to.

config_entries.label: Preset Modes
config_entries.description: A list of preset modes for this fan. Preset modes can be used in automations (i.e. `on_preset_set`  ).

config_entries.label: Speed Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive speed commands on (options: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH).

config_entries.label: Speed Count
config_entries.description: Set the number of supported discrete speed levels. The value is used to calculate the percentages for each speed. E.g. `2` means that you have 50% and 100% while `100` will allow 1% increments in the output. Defaults to `100`.

config_entries.label: Speed Level Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive numeric speed commands on (range: 0 to speed count).

config_entries.label: Speed Level State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish numeric fan speed state changes to (range: 0 to speed count).

config_entries.label: Speed State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish fan speed state changes to (options: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH).

The datasheet specifies a 10-minute preheating time for full accuracy, with 90% accuracy achieved after 3 minutes. Empirical evidence shows that reasonable values are usually returned after about 1 minute. Defaults to `75s`.

components.name: HTTP Request
components.description: The `http_request` component lets you make HTTP/HTTPS requests. To do so, you need to add it to your device's configuration:

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Buffer Size Rx
config_entries.description: Change HTTP receive buffer size. Defaults to `512`.

config_entries.label: Buffer Size Tx
config_entries.description: Change HTTP transmit buffer size. Defaults to `512`.

config_entries.label: Ca Certificate Path
config_entries.description: Path to a CA certificate bundle. Not required on MacOS (the inbuilt CA bundle is used and SSL enabled by default).

config_entries.label: Esp8266 Disable Ssl Support
config_entries.description: Determines whether to include HTTPS/SSL support in the firmware binary. Excluding the SSL libraries from your build will result in a smaller binary, which may be necessary for memory-constrained devices (512 kB or 1 MB). If you see `Error: ESP does not have enough space to store OTA file` in your device's logs, you may need to enable this option. Defaults to `false`. By setting this option to `true`  :

config_entries.label: Follow Redirects
config_entries.description: Enable following HTTP redirects. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Redirect Limit
config_entries.description: Maximum amount of redirects to follow when enabled. Defaults to `3`.

config_entries.label: Timeout
config_entries.description: Timeout for request. Defaults to `4.5s`.

config_entries.label: Tls Buffer Size Rx
config_entries.description: Change TLS receive buffer size. Should be set to `16384` to fit the TLS record size of modern HTTP servers. This will increase RAM usage significantly and may require removing other components to free up RAM. You can check the max free heap block using the [Debug Component](https://esphome.io/components/debug/). If the server is configured to support the MFL TLS extension then this can be reduced, but most popular servers (Traefik, Caddy, Cloudflare) don't support it and nginx has it disabled by default. Defaults to `512`.

config_entries.label: Tls Buffer Size Tx
config_entries.description: Change TLS transmit buffer size. Defaults to `512`.

config_entries.label: Useragent
config_entries.description: User-Agent header for requests. Defaults to `ESPHome/<version> (https://esphome.io)` where `<version>` is the version of ESPHome the device is running. For example: `ESPHome/2024.6.0 (https://esphome.io)`

config_entries.label: Verify Ssl
config_entries.description: When set to `true` (default), SSL/TLS certificates will be validated upon connection; if invalid, the connection will be aborted. To accomplish this, ESP-IDF's default ESP x509 certificate bundle is included in the build. This certificate bundle includes the complete list of root certificates from Mozilla's NSS root certificate store. **Supported on ESP32 only; must be explicitly set to false on other platforms.**

config_entries.label: Watchdog Timeout
config_entries.description: Change the watchdog timeout during connection/data transfer. May be useful on slow connections or connections with high latency. **Do not change this value unless you are experiencing device reboots due to watchdog timeouts;** doing so may prevent the device from rebooting due to a legitimate problem. **Only available on ESP32 and RP2040**.

components.name: I²C Bus
components.description: This component sets up the I²C bus for your ESP32, ESP8266, RP2040 or NRF52. In order for these components to work correctly, you need to define the I²C bus in your configuration. On ESP32 (both Arduino and ESP-IDF frameworks), internal pullup resistors are enabled by default. On ESP8266, the internal 10kΩ pullup resistors are always enabled. External pullups are still recommended for longer wire runs or multiple devices. You can use multiple devices on one I²C bus as each device is given a unique address for communicating between it and the ESP. You can do this by hopping wires from the two lines (SDA and SCL) from each device board to the next device board or by connecting the wires from each device back to the two I²C pins on the ESP.

config_entries.label: Scl
config_entries.description: The pin for the clock line of the I²C bus. Defaults to the default of your board (usually GPIO22 for ESP32 and GPIO5 for ESP8266).

config_entries.label: Sda
config_entries.description: The pin for the data line of the I²C bus. Defaults to the default of your board (usually GPIO21 for ESP32 and GPIO4 for ESP8266).

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for this I²C bus if you need multiple I²C buses.

config_entries.label: Frequency
config_entries.description: Set the frequency the I²C bus should operate on. Defaults to `50kHz`. Default for NRF52 is `100kHz`. Values are `10kHz`, `50kHz`, `100kHz`, `200kHz`, ... `800kHz`. NRF52 supports only `100kHz` and `400kHz`.

config_entries.label: Low Power Mode
config_entries.description: Enable the low-power (master only) I²C bus. Only available on ESP32C5, ESP32C6 and ESP32P4. Defaults to `false` unless required.

config_entries.label: Scan
config_entries.description: If ESPHome should do a search of the I²C address space on startup. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Scl Pullup Enabled
config_entries.description: Enable the internal pullup resistor for the SCL pin. Defaults to `true`. Only available on ESP32.

config_entries.label: Sda Pullup Enabled
config_entries.description: Enable the internal pullup resistor for the SDA pin. Defaults to `true`. Only available on ESP32.

config_entries.label: Timeout
config_entries.description: Set the I²C bus timeout. Defaults to the framework defaults (`100us` on `esp32`, `1s` on `esp8266` and `1s` on `rp2040`). Maximum on `esp32` is 13ms.

components.name: ILI9xxx TFT LCD Series
components.description: With this display driver you can control the following displays:

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: Display update frequency. Defaults to `16ms` (~60 FPS). Set to `never` when using LVGL.

config_entries.label: Model
config_entries.description: The model of the display. Options are:

config_entries.label: Cs Pin
config_entries.description: The CS pin.

config_entries.label: Dc Pin
config_entries.description: The DC pin.

config_entries.label: Invert Colors
config_entries.description: Specifies whether the display colors should be inverted. Options are `true` or `false` - if you are unsure, use `false` and change if the colors are not as expected.

config_entries.label: Reset Pin
config_entries.description: The RESET pin.

config_entries.label: Auto Clear Enabled
config_entries.description: Whether to automatically clear the display data before each lambda call, or to keep the existing display content (must overwrite explicitly, e.g., only on data change). Defaults to `true` if a lambda or pages are configured, false otherwise.

config_entries.label: Color Order
config_entries.description: Should be one of `bgr` (default) or `rgb`.

config_entries.label: Color Palette
config_entries.description: When using 8 bit colors, this controls the type of color palette that will be used in the ESP's internal 8-bits-per-pixel buffer. This can be used to improve color depth quality of the image. For example if you know that the display will only be showing grayscale images, the clarity of the display can be improved by targeting the available colors to monochrome only. Options are:

config_entries.label: Color Palette Images
config_entries.description: A list of image files that will be used to generate the color palette for the display. This should only be used in conjunction with `color_palette: IMAGE_ADAPTIVE`. The images will be analysed at compile time and a custom color palette will be created based on the most commonly occuring colors. A typical setting would be a sample image that represented the fully populated display. This can significantly improve the quality of displayed images. Note that these images are not stored on the ESP device, just the 256byte color palette created from them.

config_entries.label: Dimensions
config_entries.description: Dimensions of the screen, specified either as *width* **x** *height* (e.g `320x240`  ) or with separate config keys. If not provided the dimensions will be determined by the model selected.

config_entries.label: Height
config_entries.description: Specifies height of display in pixels.

config_entries.label: Width
config_entries.description: Specifies width of display.

config_entries.label: Offset Height
config_entries.description: Specify an offset for the y-direction of the display. Default is 0.

config_entries.label: Offset Width
config_entries.description: Specify an offset for the x-direction of the display, typically used when an LCD is smaller than the maximum supported by the driver chip. Default is 0

config_entries.label: Init Sequence
config_entries.description: Allows custom initialisation sequences to be added. See below for more information.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: The lambda to use for rendering the content on the display. `it` will be an instance of <APIClass text="DisplayBuffer" path="display::DisplayBuffer" />. See [Display Rendering Engine](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-engine) for more information.

config_entries.label: Pages
config_entries.description: Show pages instead of a single lambda. See [Display Pages](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-pages).

config_entries.label: Pixel Mode
config_entries.description: Allows forcing the display into 18 or 16 bit mode. Options are `18bit` or `16bit`. If unspecified, the pixel mode will be determined by the model choice. Not all displays will work in both modes.

config_entries.label: Rotation
config_entries.description: Rotate the display presentation in software. Choose one of `0°`, `90°`, `180°`, or `270°`. This option cannot be used with `transform`.

config_entries.label: Transform
config_entries.description: Transform the display presentation using hardware. All defaults are `false`. This option cannot be used with `rotation`.

config_entries.label: Mirror X
config_entries.description: If true, mirror the x axis.

config_entries.label: Mirror Y
config_entries.description: If true, mirror the y axis.

config_entries.label: Swap Xy
config_entries.description: If true, exchange the x and y axes.

components.name: Images
components.description: Use this component to store graphical images on the device, you can then draw the images on compatible displays.

config_entries.label: Type
config_entries.description: Specifies how to encode image internally.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The ID with which you will be able to reference the image later in your display code.

config_entries.label: File
config_entries.description: id in the format mdi:icon-name, and that icon will automatically be downloaded and added to the configuration. id in the format mdil:icon-name, and that icon will automatically be downloaded and added to the configuration. id in the format memory:icon-name, and that icon will automatically be downloaded and added to the configuration.

config_entries.label: Byte Order
config_entries.description: For RGB565 images, the pixels are converted to 16 bit values. By default these will be stored in little endian byte order (LSB first), but you can override this by setting `byte_order` to `big_endian`. Options are `little_endian` (default) and `big_endian`. Not applicable to other image formats. Images used in displays and LVGL are expected to be in little endian format.

config_entries.label: Dither
config_entries.description: Specifies which dither method used to process the image, only used in GRAYSCALE and BINARY type image. Defaults to `NONE`. You can read more about it on the [Pillow documentation](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/Image.html?highlight=Dither#PIL.Image.Image.convert) and on [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dither).

config_entries.label: Invert Alpha
config_entries.description: Applicable to binary and grayscale only, this will invert the colors, i.e. make black white and vice versa. Useful for e-ink displays. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Resize
config_entries.description: If set, this will resize the image to fit inside the given dimensions `WIDTHxHEIGHT` and preserve the aspect ratio.

config_entries.label: Transparency
config_entries.description: If set the alpha channel of the input image will be taken into account. The possible values are `opaque` (default), `chroma_key` and `alpha_channel`. Binary images do not support `alpha_channel`. See discussion on transparency below.

components.name: Improv via Serial
components.description: The `improv_serial` component in ESPHome implements the open [Improv standard](https://www.improv-wifi.com/) for configuring Wi-Fi on an ESPHome device by using a serial connection to the device, eg. USB.

config_entries.label: Next Url
config_entries.description: A URL that can be used to forward the user to after setting credentials with improv.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the sensor. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default device class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: Command
config_entries.description:
The KMP command code (e.g. 0x003C).

*See also: [Kamstrup Meter Protocol [KMP]](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/kamstrup_kmp#example-configuration-entry)*

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: State Class

components.name: Key collector component
components.description: The `key_collector` component collects key presses from components like [Matrix keypad](https://esphome.io/components/matrix_keypad#matrix_keypad), [Wiegand keypad](https://esphome.io/components/wiegand/) or LVGL [Button Matrix](https://esphome.io/components/lvgl/widgets#lvgl-widget-buttonmatrix), [Keyboard](https://esphome.io/components/lvgl/widgets#lvgl-widget-keyboard) widgets. It allows you to process key sequences and treat them as one, for example to allow inputting of a PIN code or a passkey. The component outputs the result of the keypress sequence as a variable usable in automations, and can publish the result to a `text_sensor`.

config_entries.label: Source Id
config_entries.description: The ID of the key collector component to monitor.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Set the ID of this entry for use in lambdas.

config_entries.label: Allowed Keys
config_entries.description: Keys allowed to be used. If not specified, then any otherwise unused keys will be allowed.

config_entries.label: Back Keys
config_entries.description: Keys used to delete the last pressed key. Like *Backspace* on a keyboard.

config_entries.label: Clear Keys
config_entries.description: Keys used to cancel building the key sequence.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot
config_entries.description: If enabled, this key collector will be enabled on boot. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: End Key Required
config_entries.description: Only trigger `on_result` automation when one of the `end_keys` was pressed, and not when `max_length` characters have been entered. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: End Keys
config_entries.description: Keys used to *finish* the key sequence and trigger the `on_result` automation.

config_entries.label: Max Length
config_entries.description: The maximum length of the desired key sequence. After this limit is reached, the collector will either ignore additional keys or trigger the `on_result` automation, depending on `end_key_required`.

config_entries.label: Min Length
config_entries.description: The minimum length of the desired key sequence. Below this limit, `on_result` automation will not trigger even if any of the `end_keys` was pressed.

config_entries.label: Start Keys
config_entries.description: Keys used to *start* the key sequence; when set, no keys will be accepted until one of the start keys is pressed.

config_entries.label: Timeout
config_entries.description: Timeout after which to cancel building the key sequence.

components.name: Character-Based LCD Display
components.description: The `lcd_gpio` version of this component addresses the screen directly and does not employ a GPIO expander module. Each of the data pins of the LCD needs a dedicated GPIO pin on the ESP. Connecting the screen this way offers faster refresh, especially in conjunction with an [LCD Menu](https://esphome.io/components/display_menu/lcd_menu#lcd_menu).

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to re-draw the screen. Defaults to `1s`.

config_entries.label: Data Pins
config_entries.description: A list of the data pins you have hooked up to the LCD. The list can either be 4 items long (operating in 4-bit mode with either the first 4 data pins connected or the last 4 data pins connected), or 8 items long (when you have connected all 8 data pins).

config_entries.label: Dimensions
config_entries.description: The dimensions of the display with `COLUMNSxROWS`. If you're not sure, power the display on, turn contrast high up and just count them.

config_entries.label: Enable Pin
config_entries.description: The pin you have `E` (`06`  ) hooked up to.

config_entries.label: Rs Pin
config_entries.description: The pin you have `RS` (`04`  ) hooked up to.

config_entries.label: Rw Pin
config_entries.description: Optionally set the pin you have `R/W` (`05`  ) hooked up to. You can also just permanently connect that pin to `GND`.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: The lambda to use for rendering the content on the display. See [Rendering Lambda](https://esphome.io/components/display/lcd_display#display-lcd_lambda) for more information.

components.name: LCD Menu
components.description: The component provides an infrastructure for setting up a hierarchical menu on character based LCD displays. This offers the user an interactive method to display labels, control entities like `switch`, `select`, `number`  available locally on the ESPHome node, without the requirement of a network connection.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Display Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID of the LCD display.

config_entries.label: Mark Back
config_entries.description: Code of the character used to mark menu items going back one level. As the character set lacks a good looking back arrow, using a user defined character is advisable (use `8` to reference one at position `0` to avoid problems with zeros in a string). Defaults to `0x5e` (`^`  ).

config_entries.label: Mark Editing
config_entries.description: Code of the character used to mark menu item editing mode. Defaults to `0x2a` (`*`  ).

config_entries.label: Mark Selected
config_entries.description: Code of the character used to mark menu item selected. Defaults to `0x3e` (`>`  ).

config_entries.label: Mark Submenu
config_entries.description: Code of the character used to mark menu item leading to a submenu. Defaults to `0x7e` (a right arrow).

components.name: Character-Based LCD Display
components.description: `lcd_pcf8574` is for LCD displays with a PCF8574 GPIO expander module connected to all the data pins. The communication happens via [I²C Bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c), you need to have an `i2c:` section in your configuration.

config_entries.description: The [I²C](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) address of the PCF8574 chip, defaults to `0x3F`.

config_entries.description: The interval to re-draw the screen. Defaults to `1s`.

config_entries.description: The dimensions of the display with `COLUMNSxROWS`. If you're not sure, power the display up and just count them.

components.name: MCP230xx I/O Expander
components.description: The MCP23008 component ([datasheet](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/MCP23008-MCP23S08-Data-Sheet-DS20001919.pdf), [Adafruit](https://www.adafruit.com/product/593)) has 8 GPIOs that can be configured independently.

config_entries.description: The I²C address of the driver. Defaults to `0x20`.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The id to use for this MCP23008 component.

config_entries.label: Interrupt Pin
config_entries.description: The pin connected to the INT output of the MCP23008. When configured, the component becomes interrupt-driven instead of polling — it only reads the chip when a pin actually changes state, significantly reducing I²C bus traffic and CPU usage. Must be an internal GPIO pin (not another expander pin).

config_entries.label: Open Drain Interrupt
config_entries.description: Configure the interrupt pin to open-drain mode. Useful when the MCP23008's power supply is greater than 3.3 volts. Note that this pin will require a pull-up resistor (to 3.3 volts) when this mode is enabled.

components.name: Modbus Component
components.description: The Modbus protocol is used by many consumer and industrial devices for communication. This component allows components in ESPHome to communicate to those devices via RTU protocol. You can access the coils, inputs, holding, read registers from your devices as sensors, switches, selects, numbers or various other ESPHome components and present them to your favorite Home Automation system. You can even write them as binary or float ouptputs from ESPHome.

config_entries.label: Flow Control Pin
config_entries.description: The pin used to switch flow control. This is useful for RS485 transceivers that do not have automatic flow control switching, like the common MAX485. If your UART supports `flow_control_pin`, you should configure this in the `uart` component, not in the `modbus` component.

config_entries.label: Uart Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID of the [UART Component](https://esphome.io/components/uart) if you want to use multiple UART buses.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Disable Crc
config_entries.description: If set to `true`, invalid CRC values are ignored. This will reduce error messages but will not fix communication issues. Try increasing times above first if you see CRC errors. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Role
config_entries.description: The role of this component, `client` or `server`. Defaults to `client`.

config_entries.label: Send Wait Time
config_entries.description: Time in milliseconds before the next ModBUS command is sent when an answer from a previous command has not yet started (i.e. when to timeout and assume no response is coming). Defaults to 250 ms. Set this value to the maximum time required for the slowest device on the bus to begin responding (time to first byte). If a device starts responding within this time, the next command will be queued and sent after the response is finished, no matter how long the response.

config_entries.label: Turnaround Time
config_entries.description: Time in milliseconds before the next ModBUS command is sent after last response is received. This interval allows other devices on the bus time to process messages. Defaults to 100 ms. This value is ideally set to the maximum time required for the slowest device on the bus to process a message and be ready to process another. Note that all devices will receive all messages and will require time to process them even if they don't need to reply. If devices don't respond sometimes, it can help to increase this value.

components.name: Modbus Controller
components.description: The `modbus_controller` component creates a RS485 connection to either:

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: start address of the first register in a range (can be decimal or hexadecimal).

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval that the sensors should be checked. Defaults to 60 seconds.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Allow Duplicate Commands
config_entries.description: Whether to allow duplicate commands in the queue. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Command Throttle
config_entries.description: minimum time in between 2 requests to the device. Default is `0ms`. Some Modbus slave devices limit the rate of requests from the master, so this allows the interval between requests to be altered.

config_entries.label: Max Cmd Retries
config_entries.description: How many times a command will be retried if no response is received. It doesn't include the initial transmition. Defaults to 4.

config_entries.label: Modbus Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID of the `modbus` hub.

config_entries.label: Offline Skip Updates
config_entries.description: When a slave doesn't respond to a command, it is marked as offline, you can specify how many updates will be skipped while it is offline. If using a bus with multiple slaves, this avoids waiting for timeouts allowing to read other slaves in the same bus. When the slave responds to a command, it'll be marked online again.

config_entries.label: Server Courtesy Response
config_entries.description: Configuration block to enable the courtesy response feature when the device is acting as a Modbus server.

config_entries.label: Enabled
config_entries.description: Whether to enable the courtesy response feature. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Register Last Address
config_entries.description: The highest Modbus register address (inclusive) up to which undefined registers are allowed to be read and will be padded with a default value. Any read request that includes undefined registers within this range will return the value specified by `register_value` instead of triggering an exception. Defaults to `65535`

config_entries.label: Register Value
config_entries.description: The 16-bit value (range: 0–65535) to return for undefined registers within the address range defined by `register_last_address`. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Server Registers
config_entries.description: A list of registers that are responded to when acting as a server.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: start address of the first register in a range

config_entries.label: Read Lambda
config_entries.description: Lambda that returns the value of this register.

config_entries.label: Value Type
config_entries.description: datatype of the mod_bus register data. The default data type for ModBUS is a 16 bit integer in **big endian** format (network byte order, MSB first)

config_entries.label: Write Lambda
config_entries.description: Lambda that sets the value of this register. A variable `x` of the appropriate type (`uint16_t`, `int32_t`, etc, see above) is provided with the value, as well as `address` containing the address of this register. You must return `true` if the operation was successful, `false` otherwise, in which case a ModBUS exception code `4` will be sent to the client.

config_entries.description: sometimes multiple values are packed in a single register's response. The bitmask is used to determined if the result is true or false. See Bitmasks.

config_entries.description: raw bytes for modbus command. This allows using non-standard commands. If custom_command is used address and register_type can't be used. Custom data must contain all required bytes including the modbus device address. The CRC is automatically calculated and appended to the command. See Using custom_command how to use custom_command.

config_entries.description: A list of filters to apply on the binary sensor values such as inverting signals. See [Binary Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/binary_sensor#binary_sensor-filters).

config_entries.label: Force New Range
config_entries.description: If possible sensors with sequential addresses are grouped together and requested in one range. Setting force_new_range: true enforces the start of a new range at that address.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: Lambda to be evaluated every update interval to get the new value of the sensor. Parameters: Possible return values for the lambda.

config_entries.label: Offset
config_entries.description: Offset from start address in bytes (only required for uncommon response encodings). If more than one register is written in a command, this value is used to find the start of this datapoint relative to the start address. The component calculates the size of the range based on offset and size of the value type. The value for offset depends on the register type. If a binary_sensor is created from an input register, the offset is in bytes. For coil and discrete input resisters, the LSB of the first data byte contains the coil addressed in the request. The other coils follow toward the high-order end of this byte and from low order to high order in subsequent bytes. For registers, the offset is the position of the relevant bit. To get the value of the coil register, 2 can be retrieved using address: 2 / offset: 0 or address: 0 / offset 2.

config_entries.label: Register Type
config_entries.description: type of the modbus register.

config_entries.label: Response Size
config_entries.description: Size of the response for the register in bytes. Defaults to register_count*2.

config_entries.label: Skip Updates
config_entries.description: By default all sensors of a modbus_controller are updated together. For data points that don't change very frequently updates can be skipped. A value of 5 would only update this sensor range in every 6th update cycle. Note: The modbus_controller groups components by address ranges to reduce number of transactions. All components with the same starting address will be updated in one request. skip_updates applies for all components in the same range.

config_entries.label: Trigger On Initial State
config_entries.description: If true, any applicable triggers will be fired when the binary sensor state changes from `unknown` to a valid state. This applies to the first valid state set, and any valid state set after a `binary_sensor.invalidate_state` action has been executed. The default is `false`.

components.description: The `mpr121` sensor platform allows you to use your MPR121 ([datasheet](https://cdn-learn.adafruit.com/downloads/pdf/adafruit-mpr121-12-key-capacitive-touch-sensor-breakout-tutorial.pdf), [Adafruit](https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-mpr121-12-key-capacitive-touch-sensor-breakout-tutorial/overview)) Capacitive Touch Sensor with ESPHome. config_entries.description: Set the ID of this sensor.

config_entries.description: The minimum length that no touch is recognized before a release event is created. Range is from 0 to 7. Defaults to 0.

config_entries.description: The release defines the sensitivity for touch detection and should be between 5 and 30. Defaults to 6.

config_entries.label: Touch Debounce
config_entries.description: The minimum length before a touch is recognized. Range is from 0 to 7. Defaults to 0.

config_entries.label: Touch Threshold
config_entries.description: The touch threshold for all channels. This defines the sensitivity for touch detection and should be between 5 and 30 (lower = more sensitive). Defaults to 12. Typically the touch threshold is a little bigger than the release threshold.

components.name: MQTT Client Component
components.description: The MQTT Client Component sets up the MQTT connection to your broker. If you are connecting to Home Assistant, you may prefer to use the native API, in which case this is not needed.

config_entries.label: Password
config_entries.description: The password to use for authentication. Empty (the default) means no authentication.

config_entries.label: Broker
config_entries.description: The host of your MQTT broker.

config_entries.label: Username
config_entries.description: The username to use for authentication. Empty (the default) means no authentication.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Birth Message
config_entries.description: The message to send when a connection to the broker is established. See [Last Will And Birth Messages](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt#mqtt-last_will_birth) for more information.

config_entries.label: Certificate Authority
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. CA certificate in PEM format. See [TLS (ESP32)](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt#mqtt-tls-idf) for more information.

config_entries.label: Clean Session
config_entries.description: Whether the broker will clean the MQTT session after disconnect. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Client Certificate
config_entries.description: Only on `esp32`. Client certificate in PEM format.

config_entries.label: Client Certificate Key
config_entries.description: Only on `esp32`. Client private key in PEM format.

config_entries.label: Client Id
config_entries.description: The client id to use for opening connections. See [Defaults](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt#mqtt-defaults) for more information.

config_entries.label: Discover Ip
config_entries.description: If Home Assistant automatic device discovery should be enabled. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Discovery
config_entries.description: Manually enable/disable

config_entries.label: Discovery Object Id Generator
config_entries.description: The object_id generator to use. Can be one of `none` or `device_name`. Defaults to `none` which does not generate object_id. `device_name` generator uses format `<device_name>_<friendly_name>`.

config_entries.label: Discovery Prefix
config_entries.description: The prefix to use for Home Assistant's MQTT discovery. Should not contain trailing slash. Defaults to `homeassistant`.

config_entries.label: Discovery Retain
config_entries.description: Whether to retain MQTT discovery messages so that entities are added automatically on Home Assistant restart. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Discovery Unique Id Generator
config_entries.description: The unique_id generator to use. Can be one of `legacy` or `mac`. Defaults to `legacy`, which generates unique_id in format `ESP<component_type><default_object_id>`. `mac` generator uses format `<mac_address>-<component_type>-<fnv1_hash(friendly_name)>`.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot
config_entries.description: If enabled, MQTT will be enabled on boot. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Idf Send Async
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. If true publishing the message happens from a separate mqtt task. The client only enqueues the message. Defaults to `false`. config_entries.label: Keepalive
config_entries.description: The time to keep the MQTT socket alive, decreasing this can help with overall stability due to more WiFi traffic with more pings. Defaults to 15 seconds.
