config_entries.label: Port
config_entries.description: Port of the ESPHome API (if enabled).

config_entries.label: Publish Nan As None
config_entries.description: Publish `None` instead of `NaN` to handle Unknown/Unavailable sensor states in Home Assistant. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Reboot Timeout
config_entries.description: The amount of time to wait before rebooting when no MQTT connection exists. Can be disabled by setting this to `0s`. Defaults to `15min`.

config_entries.label: Shutdown Message
config_entries.description: The message to send when the node shuts down and the connection is closed cleanly. See [Last Will And Birth Messages](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt#mqtt-last_will_birth) for more information.

config_entries.label: Skip Cert Cn Check
config_entries.description: Only on ESP32. Don't verify if the common name in the server certificate matches the value of `broker`.

config_entries.label: Topic Prefix
config_entries.description: The prefix used for all MQTT messages. Should not contain trailing slash. Defaults to `<APP_NAME>`. Use `null` to disable publishing or subscribing of any MQTT topic unless it is explicitly configured.

config_entries.label: Use Abbreviations

config_entries.label: Wait For Connection
config_entries.description: Blocks other components from starting until the MQTT connection is established. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Will Message

config_entries.description: If set to `true`, the Nextion will be configured to wake from sleep when touched.

config_entries.label: Brightness
config_entries.description: When specified, the display brightness will be set to this value at boot.

config_entries.label: Command Spacing
config_entries.description: Sets the minimum time between commands sent to the Nextion display. A higher value can help prevent buffer overflows but will result in slower interface updates. Range is `0-255ms`. Defaults to `0ms` (disabled).

config_entries.label: Dump Device Info
config_entries.description: Shows device information (model, firmware version, serial number, flash size) in the configuration dump. When disabled, device info is only logged during connection establishment to save memory. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Exit Reparse On Start
config_entries.description: Request the Nextion exit Active Reparse Mode before setup of the display. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: The lambda to use for rendering the content on the Nextion display. See [Rendering Lambda](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#display-nextion_lambda) for more information. This is typically empty. The individual components for the Nextion will handle almost all functions needed for updating display elements.

config_entries.label: Max Commands Per Loop
config_entries.description: Limits the number of commands processed per loop cycle. This helps prevent stack overflows when a large number of commands are queued. Lower values (for example, `20`  ) may help improve stability in constrained environments.

config_entries.label: Max Queue Age
config_entries.description: Maximum age in milliseconds for queued commands before they are automatically removed. This helps prevent stale commands from being executed after delays. Set to ``0`` to disable age-based removal (commands are only limited by queue size). **Note:** Very low values (e.g., \<50ms) may cause commands to be dropped before transmission due to ESPHome's loop timing (~16ms). Recommended minimum is 100ms when enabled. Range: 0-65535. Defaults to ``8000`` (8 seconds).

config_entries.label: Max Queue Size
config_entries.description: Sets the maximum number of commands that can be queued at once. When the limit is reached, new commands will be dropped and a warning will be logged. This helps prevent memory overflows or boot-time crashes in complex setups that issue a large number of commands in rapid succession. If not set, the queue size is unlimited.

config_entries.label: Skip Connection Handshake
config_entries.description: Sets whether the initial display connection handshake process is skipped. When set to `true`, the connection will be established without performing the handshake. This can be useful when using Nextion Simulator. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Start Up Page
config_entries.description: Sets the page to display when ESPHome connects to the Nextion. (Nextion shows page 0 on start-up by default).

config_entries.label: Startup Override Ms
config_entries.description: Time in milliseconds to wait before forcing the display to be marked as ready if it hasn't responded to the connection handshake. Set to ``0`` to disable the override and wait indefinitely for the handshake. This is useful for displays with slower startup sequences or to enforce strict handshake requirements. Range: 0-65535. Defaults to ``8000`` (8 seconds).

config_entries.label: Tft Upload Http Retries
config_entries.description: Number of retries for transient HTTP failures during TFT upload. On Arduino, this applies to the initial connection request. On ESP-IDF, this applies to chunk read operations. Range: 1-255. Defaults to `5`.

config_entries.label: Tft Upload Http Timeout
config_entries.description: HTTP request timeout for TFT upload transfers. Applies to each individual HTTP request during the upload process. Range: 1-65535ms. Defaults to `4.5s`.

config_entries.label: Tft Upload Watchdog Timeout
config_entries.description: Temporarily adjusts the system watchdog timeout for the duration of the TFT transfer process. The original timeout is automatically restored when the transfer completes (whether successful or not). May be useful on slow connections or when transferring large TFT files. Do not set this unless you are experiencing device reboots due to watchdog timeouts during TFT uploads; doing so may prevent the device from rebooting due to a legitimate problem. Only available on ESP32.

config_entries.label: Tft Url
config_entries.description: The URL from which to download the TFT file for display firmware updates (Nextion OTA). See [Nextion Upload](https://esphome.io/components/display/nextion#nextion_upload_tft).

config_entries.label: Touch Sleep Timeout
config_entries.description: Sets internal No-touch-then-sleep timer in seconds. Range: 0 (disabled) or 3-65535 seconds (max: ~18 hours). Values 1-2 are auto-corrected to 3. When set, Nextion will automatically enter sleep mode after the specified period of no touch activity. This setting persists until device reboot or reset. Note: The display will only wake up by restart or by configuring `auto_wake_on_touch: true`.

config_entries.label: Wake Up Page
config_entries.description: Sets the page to display after waking up

components.name: OpenTherm
components.description: OpenTherm (OT) is a standard communications protocol used in central heating systems for the communication between central heating appliances and a thermostatic controller. As a standard, OpenTherm is independent of any single manufacturer. A controller from manufacturer A can in principle be used to control a boiler from manufacturer B.

config_entries.label: Out Pin

config_entries.label: Opentherm Version Controller
config_entries.description: Version of OpenTherm implemented by controller

config_entries.label: Sync Mode
config_entries.description: Synchronous communication mode prevents other components from disabling interrupts while we are talking to the boiler. Enable if you experience a lot of random intermittent invalid response errors (very likely to happen while using Dallas temperature sensors).

components.name: OpenTherm
components.description: The component can report boiler status on several binary sensors. The *Status* sensors are updated in each message cycle, while the others are only set during initialization, as they are unlikely to change without restarting the boiler.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default device class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: State Class
config_entries.description: The state class for the sensor. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default state class of a sensor.

The INT pin is active-low and open-drain, so an external or internal pull-up resistor is required. Must be an internal GPIO pin (not another expander pin).

components.name: PID Climate
components.description: The `pid` climate platform allows you to regulate a value with a [PID controller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PID_controller).

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the climate device. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the climate device in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Control Parameters
config_entries.description: Control parameters of the PID controller.

config_entries.label: Kp
config_entries.description: The factor for the proportional term of the PID controller.

config_entries.label: Derivative Averaging Samples
config_entries.description: average the derivative term over this many samples. Many controllers don't use the derivative term because it is sensitive to slight changes in the input sensor. By taking an average of the derivative term it might become more useful for you. Most PID controllers call this derivative filtering. The derivative term is used to pre-act so don't filter too much. Defaults to `1` which is no sampling/averaging.

config_entries.label: Kd
config_entries.description: The factor for the derivative term of the PID controller. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Ki
config_entries.description: The factor for the integral term of the PID controller. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Max Integral
config_entries.description: The maximum value of the integral term multiplied by `ki` to prevent windup. Defaults to `1`.

config_entries.label: Min Integral
config_entries.description: The minimum value of the integral term multiplied by `ki` to prevent windup. Defaults to `-1`.

config_entries.label: Output Averaging Samples
config_entries.description: average the output over this many samples. PID controllers can be quite sensitive to small changes on the input sensor. By averaging the last X output samples, the temperature can be more stable. However, the larger the sampling window, the less responsive the PID controller. Defaults to `1` which is no sampling/averaging.

config_entries.label: Starting Integral Term
config_entries.description: Set the initial output, by priming the integral term. This is useful for when your system is rebooted and you don't want to wait for it to get back equilibrium.

config_entries.label: Cool Output
config_entries.description: The ID of a [float output](https://esphome.io/components/output#config-output) that decreases the current temperature. At least one of `heat_output` and `cool_output` must be specified.

config_entries.label: Default Target Temperature
config_entries.description: The default target temperature (setpoint) for the control algorithm. This can be dynamically set in the frontend later.

config_entries.label: Heat Output
config_entries.description: The ID of a [float output](https://esphome.io/components/output#config-output) that increases the current temperature. At least one of `heat_output` and `cool_output` must be specified.

config_entries.label: Humidity Sensor
config_entries.description: If specified, this sensor is used to measure the current humidity. This is used for information only and does not influence temperature control.

config_entries.label: Sensor
config_entries.description: The sensor that is used to measure the current temperature.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Action State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish climate device action changes to.

config_entries.label: Current Humidity State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish current humidity changes to.

config_entries.label: Current Temperature State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish current temperature changes to.

config_entries.label: Deadband Parameters
config_entries.description: Enables a deadband to stabilise and minimise changes in the output when the temperature is close to the target temperature. See [Deadband Setup](https://esphome.io/components/climate/pid#deadband-setup).

config_entries.label: Deadband Output Averaging Samples
config_entries.description: Typically when inside the deadband the PID Controller has reached a state of equilibrium, so it advantageous to use a higher number of output samples like 10-30 samples. Defaults to `1` which is no sampling/averaging.

config_entries.label: Kd Multiplier
config_entries.description: Set the `kd` gain when inside the deadband. Recommended this is set to `0`. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Ki Multiplier
config_entries.description: Set the `ki` gain when inside the deadband. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Kp Multiplier
config_entries.description: Set the `kp` gain when inside the deadband. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default

components.name: PMWCS3 Capacitive Soil Moisture and Temperature Sensor
components.description: The `pmwcs3` sensor platform allows you to use your PMWCS3 ([informations](https://tinovi.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/PM-WCS-3-I2C.pdf)) capacitive soil moisture and temperature sensor with ESPHome. The [I²C bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) is required to be set up in your configuration for this sensor to work. Wiring scheme: red is 3.3V, black & shield is GND, green is SDA and white is SCL. 2.2kOhm resistors are advised to pullup both SDA & SDA lines.

config_entries.description: Manually specify the I²C address of the sensor. Defaults to `0x63`.

components.name: Power Supply Component
components.description: The `power_supply` component allows you to have a high power mode for certain outputs. For example, if you're using an [ATX powersupply](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATX) to power your LED strips, you usually don't want to have the power supply on all the time while the output is not on. The power supply component can be attached to any [Output Component](https://esphome.io/components/output/) and will automatically switch on if any of the outputs are on. Furthermore, it also has a cooldown time that keeps the power supply on for a while after the last output has been disabled.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The GPIO pin to control the power supply on.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The id of the power supply so that it can be used by the outputs.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot
config_entries.description: If the power supply should be enabled when the power supply component is setup. Defaults to false. The startup delay will be applied (other component setup will be blocked until the delay has elapsed.) This is useful for power supplies that will never be turned off and avoids the need to specifically configure the power supply in a different component.

config_entries.label: Enable Time
config_entries.description: The time that the power supply needs for startup. The output component will wait for this period of time after turning on the PSU and before switching the output on. Defaults to `20ms`. Maximum of less than `5s`.

config_entries.label: Keep On Time
config_entries.description: The time the power supply should be kept enabled after the last output that used it has been switch off. Defaults to `10s`.

It is intended to be a drop-in replacement for the [pulse counter component](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/pulse_counter/). Rather than counting pulses over a fixed time interval, the pulse meter sensor measures the time between pulses. The precise manner in which this is done depends on the `internal_filter_mode` option. This leads to a higher resolution, especially for low pulse rates, as the pulse counter sensor is limited by the number of pulses within a time interval.

config_entries.label: Filters

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. config_entries.label: Internal

config_entries.label: Internal Filter
config_entries.description: If a pulse shorter than this time is detected, it is discarded. Defaults to `13us`. This acts as a debounce filter to eliminate input noise, so choose a value a little less than your expected minimum pulse width.

config_entries.label: Internal Filter Mode
config_entries.description: Determines how the internal filter is applied. One of `EDGE` or `PULSE`. Defaults to `EDGE`.

config_entries.label: Timeout

config_entries.label: Total

config_entries.label: Validity Period

components.name: QMC5883L Magnetometer
components.description: The `qmc5883l` allows you to use your QMC5883L triple-axis magnetometers ([datasheet](http://wiki.sunfounder.cc/images/7/72/QMC5883L-Datasheet-1.0.pdf)) with ESPHome. This sensor is very similar to the [HMC5883L](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/hmc5883l#hmc5883l) sensor and is often found as a knock off replacement. The QMC5883L sensor performs on par to the HMC5883L sensor, though the configuration differs. The [I²C Bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) is required to be set up in your configuration for this sensor to work.

components.name: Remote Receiver
components.description: The `remote_receiver` component lets you receive and decode various common remote control signals, such as infrared or 433 MHz radio frequency (RF) signals.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The pin to receive the remote signal on.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation. Useful when multiple receivers are configured on a single device.

config_entries.label: Buffer Size
config_entries.description: The size of the internal buffer for storing the remote codes. Defaults to `10kB` on the ESP32 and `1kB` on the ESP8266.

config_entries.label: Carrier Duty Percent
config_entries.description: The carrier duty cycle for signal demodulation in the RMT peripheral in Hz. Defaults to `100`.

config_entries.label: Carrier Frequency
config_entries.description: The carrier frequency for signal demodulation in the RMT peripheral in Hz. Defaults to `0Hz` (carrier demodulation disabled).

config_entries.label: Clock Resolution
config_entries.description: The clock resolution used by the RMT peripheral in Hz. Defaults to `1000000`.

config_entries.label: Dump
config_entries.description: Decode and dump these remote codes in the logs (at log.level=DEBUG). Set to `all` to dump all available codecs:

config_entries.label: Filter
config_entries.description: Filter any pulses that are shorter than this. Useful for removing glitches from noisy signals. Allowed values are in range `0` to `4294967295us`. Defaults to `50us`.

config_entries.label: Filter Symbols
config_entries.description: Filter out any data received with a length in symbols less than `filter_symbols`. Useful for filtering out short bursts of noise.

config_entries.label: Idle
config_entries.description: The amount of time that a signal should remain stable/unchanged for it to be considered complete. Defaults to `10ms`. The maximum allowable value is:

config_entries.label: Receive Symbols
config_entries.description: Maximum receive length in symbols. On some variants the maximum receive is limited to `rmt_symbols`.

config_entries.label: Rmt Symbols
config_entries.description: When `use_dma` is enabled, this sets the size of the driver's internal DMA buffer. When DMA is disabled, it specifies how much RMT memory is allocated to the component. RMT memory is shared across all components and should be allocated in multiples of the block size. On the `ESP32` and `ESP32-S2` variants, RMT memory is shared between RX and TX components. On other variants, RX and TX have dedicated RMT memory.

config_entries.label: Tolerance
config_entries.description: The percentage or time that the remote signal lengths can deviate in the decoding process. Defaults to `25%`.

config_entries.label: Use Dma
config_entries.description: Enable DMA on variants that support it. If enabled `rmt_symbols` controls the DMA buffer size and can be set to a large value.

components.name: Remote Transmitter
components.description: The `remote_transmitter` component lets you send various common remote control signals, such as infrared or 433 MHz radio frequency (RF) signals.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The pin to transmit the remote signal on.

config_entries.label: Carrier Duty Percent
config_entries.description: How much of the time the remote is on. For example, infrared protocols modulate the signal using a carrier signal. Set this to `50%` if you're using IR LEDs and `100%` for RF applications like 433 MHz transmitters.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation. Useful when multiple transmitters are connected to a single device.

config_entries.label: Clock Resolution
config_entries.description: The clock resolution used by the RMT peripheral in Hz. Defaults to `1000000`.

config_entries.label: Eot Level
config_entries.description: Overrides the default end of transmit level. Defaults to `false` unless `pin` is set to inverted or open-drain.

config_entries.label: Non Blocking
config_entries.description: If enabled, any transmit will return immediately and the RMT will run in the background. The `on_complete` automation will trigger after the transmit completes. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Rmt Symbols
config_entries.description: When `use_dma` is enabled, this sets the size of the driver's internal DMA buffer. When DMA is disabled, it specifies how much RMT memory is allocated to the component. RMT memory is shared across all components and should be allocated in multiples of the block size. On the `ESP32` and `ESP32-S2` variants, RMT memory is shared between RX and TX components. On other variants, RX and TX have dedicated RMT memory.

config_entries.label: Use Dma
config_entries.description: Enable DMA on variants that support it. If enabled `rmt_symbols` controls the DMA buffer size and can be set to a large value.

config_entries.label: Bits Per Sample
config_entries.description: The audio sample bit depth after resampling. Defaults to the output speaker's bits per sample.

config_entries.label: Buffer Duration
config_entries.description: The duration of the internal ring buffer. Larger values may reduce stuttering but use more memory. Defaults to `500ms`.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: The number of windowed sinc interpolation filters to use. Must be between `2` and `1024`. Defaults to `16`.

config_entries.description: Sample rate to convert to. Must be between `8000` and `48000`. Defaults to the output speaker's sample rate.

components.name: RP2040 Platform
components.description: This component contains platform-specific options for the RP2040 platform.

config_entries.label: Enable Full Printf
config_entries.description: Enable full `FILE*`-based printf support. By default, ESPHome wraps `printf()`, `vprintf()`, and `fprintf()` with lightweight stubs that use `vsnprintf()` + `fwrite()`, saving ~9.2 KB of flash. ESPHome logging uses `snprintf`/`vsnprintf`, not libc printf, so these functions are typically unused unless an external component calls them. Set to `true` only if an external component needs full `FILE*`-based printf. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Watchdog Timeout
config_entries.description: The timeout to apply to the RP2040 watchdog. When the device hangs for that period of time, it will reboot. Defaults to `8388ms` (maximum). Set to `0s` to disable the watchdog entirely.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot

components.name: Safe Mode

components.name: SDL Binary Sensor
components.description: The `sdl` binary sensor platform creates a binary sensor from keyboard presses on the host platform. The sensor will be true when the key is pressed.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/binary_sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/binary_sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

components.name: SDL2 Display on host platform
components.description: The `sdl` display platform allows you to use create an ESPHome display on a desktop system running Linux or MacOS. This is particularly useful for designing display layouts, since compiling and running a host binary is much faster than compiling for and flashing a microcontroller target system.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to re-draw the screen. Defaults to `1s`.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Auto Clear Enabled
config_entries.description: Whether to automatically clear the display data before each lambda call, or to keep the existing display content (must overwrite explicitly, e.g., only on data change). Defaults to `true` if a lambda or pages are configured, false otherwise.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: The lambda to use for rendering the content on the display. See [Display Rendering Engine](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-engine) for more information.

config_entries.label: Pages
config_entries.description: Show pages instead of a single lambda. See [Display Pages](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-pages).

config_entries.label: Rotation
config_entries.description: Set the rotation of the display. Everything you draw in `lambda:` will be rotated by this option. One of `0°` (default), `90°`, `180°`, `270°`.

config_entries.label: Sdl Options
config_entries.description: Build arguments if required to specify include or library paths. Should not be required if SDL2 is properly installed.

config_entries.label: Window Options
config_entries.description: Options that affect how the display renders on the host system. All default to false, except position, which defaults to SDL's undefined position

config_entries.label: Always On Top
config_entries.description: Whether to always draw the display window above other windows or not

config_entries.label: Borderless
config_entries.description: Whether to draw the display window with or without borders

config_entries.label: Fullscreen
config_entries.description: Whether to draw the display window in fullscreen or not. This may resize the resolution of the host display to match the SDL display dimensions

config_entries.label: Resizable
config_entries.description: Whether the display window can be manually resized

config_entries.label: Skip Taskbar
config_entries.description: Whether to skip adding a taskbar icon for the display window or not

components.name: SDL2 Touch Screen Emulator
components.description: The `sdl` touchscreen platform allows emulating a touch screen by using the mouse with the `sdl` display driver. The `sdl` display component must be configured to use this.

config_entries.description: The raw value corresponding to the right

config_entries.description: The raw value corresponding to the left

config_entries.label: Y Max
config_entries.description: The raw value corresponding to the bottom

config_entries.label: Y Min
config_entries.description: The raw value corresponding to the top

config_entries.label: Display
config_entries.description: The display to use this touchscreen with.

config_entries.label: Touch Timeout
config_entries.description: A timeout for touchscreens that do not report the end of touch. The default varies depending on the touchscreen.

config_entries.label: Transform
config_entries.description: Transform the touchscreen presentation using hardware. All defaults are `false`.

config_entries.label: Mirror X
config_entries.description: If true, mirror the x axis.

config_entries.label: Mirror Y
config_entries.description: If true, mirror the y axis.

config_entries.label: Swap Xy
config_entries.description: If true, exchange the x and y axes.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: Manually specify the I²C address of the sensor. Defaults to `0x69`.

config_entries.label: Acceleration Mode
config_entries.description: Allowed value are `low`, `medium` and `high`. (default is `low`  ) By default, the RH/T acceleration algorithm is optimized for a sensor which is positioned in free air. If the sensor is integrated into another device, the ambient RH/T output values might not be optimal due to different thermal behavior. This parameter can be used to adapt the RH/T acceleration behavior for the actual use-case, leading in an improvement of the ambient RH/T output accuracy. components.name: Servo Component
components.description: The `servo` component allows you to use servo motors with ESPHome. Servos are motor controllers that contain all the electronics necessary for driving the motor and provide a simple PWM interface to control the motor.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The ID of this servo so that it can be controlled.

config_entries.label: Output
config_entries.description: The ID of the [output component](https://esphome.io/components/output/) to use for this servo.

config_entries.label: Auto Detach Time
config_entries.description: The time after reaching the target value when the servo will be detached, if set to zero, servo will not be detached. Defaults to `0s`.

config_entries.label: Idle Level
config_entries.description: The PWM duty cycle the idle value (0%) will map to. This is also the state of the servo at startup. Defaults to `7.5%`.

config_entries.label: Max Level
config_entries.description: The PWM duty cycle the maximum value (100%) will map to. Defaults to `12.0%`.

config_entries.label: Min Level
config_entries.description: The PWM duty cycle the minimum value (-100%) will map to. Defaults to `3%`.

config_entries.label: Restore
config_entries.description: Whether to restore the state of the servo motor at startup. This is useful if you have an absolute servo motor and it goes back to its 0 position at startup. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Transition Length
config_entries.description: The time needed for a full movement (-1.0 to 1.0). This will effectively limit the speed of the servo, the larger the value, the slowest the servo will move. Defaults to `0s`. This can slow down the servo to avoid loud noises or just make the movement not jerking.

components.name: SGP40 Volatile Organic Compound Sensor and SGP41 VOC and NOx Sensor
components.description: The `sgp4x` sensor platform allows you to use your Sensirion SGP40 ([datasheet](https://sensirion.com/media/documents/296373BB/6203C5DF/Sensirion_Gas_Sensors_Datasheet_SGP40.pdf)) or SGP41 ([datasheet](https://sensirion.com/media/documents/5FE8673C/61E96F50/Sensirion_Gas_Sensors_Datasheet_SGP41.pdf)) with ESPHome. The type of sensor used is automatically detected. The [I²C Bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) is required to be set up in your configuration for this sensor to work.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to check the sensor. Defaults to `60s`

config_entries.label: Compensation
config_entries.description: The block containing sensors used for compensation. If not set defaults will be used.

config_entries.label: Humidity Source
config_entries.description: Give an external humidity sensor ID here. This can improve the sensor's internal calculations.

config_entries.label: Temperature Source
config_entries.description: Give an external temperature sensor ID here. This can improve the sensor's internal calculations.

config_entries.label: Nox
config_entries.description: NOx Index. Only available with SGP41. If a SGP40 sensor is detected this sensor will be ignored

config_entries.label: Algorithm Tuning
config_entries.description: The NOx algorithm can be customized by tuning 5 different parameters.For more details see [Engineering Guidelines for SEN5x](https://sensirion.com/media/documents/25AB572C/62B463AA/Sensirion_Engineering_Guidelines_SEN5x.pdf)

config_entries.label: Gain Factor
config_entries.description: Gain factor to amplify or to attenuate the VOC index output. Allowed values are in range 1..1000. The default value is 230.

config_entries.label: Gating Max Duration Minutes
config_entries.description: Maximum duration of gating in minutes (freeze of estimator during high NOx index signal). Zero disables the gating. Allowed values are in range 0..3000. The default value is 180 minutes

config_entries.label: Index Offset
config_entries.description: NOx index representing typical (average) conditions. Allowed values are in range 1..250. The default value is 100.

config_entries.label: Learning Time Gain Hours
config_entries.description: Time constant to estimate the NOx algorithm gain from the history in hours. Past events will be forgotten after about twice the learning time. Allowed values are in range 1..1000. The default value is 12 hours.

config_entries.label: Learning Time Offset Hours
config_entries.description: Time constant to estimate the NOx algorithm offset from the history in hours. Past events will be forgotten after about twice the learning time. Allowed values are in range 1..1000. The default value is 12 hour

config_entries.label: Std Initial
config_entries.description: The initial estimate for standard deviation parameter has no impact for NOx. This parameter is still in place for consistency reasons with the VOC tuning parameters command. This parameter must always be set to 50.

config_entries.label: Store Baseline
config_entries.description: Stores and retrieves the baseline information for quicker startups. Defaults to `true`

config_entries.label: Voc
config_entries.description: VOC Index

config_entries.label: Algorithm Tuning
config_entries.description: The VOC algorithm can be customized by tuning 6 different parameters. For more details see [Engineering Guidelines for SEN5x](https://sensirion.com/media/documents/25AB572C/62B463AA/Sensirion_Engineering_Guidelines_SEN5x.pdf)

config_entries.label: Gain Factor
config_entries.description: Gain factor to amplify or to attenuate the VOC index output. Allowed values are in range 1..1000. The default value is 230.

config_entries.label: Gating Max Duration Minutes
config_entries.description: Maximum duration of gating in minutes (freeze of estimator during high VOC index signal). Zero disables the gating. Allowed values are in range 0..3000. The default value is 180 minutes

config_entries.label: Index Offset
config_entries.description: VOC index representing typical (average) conditions. Allowed values are in range 1..250. The default value is 100.

config_entries.label: Learning Time Gain Hours
config_entries.description: Time constant to estimate the VOC algorithm gain from the history in hours. Past events will be forgotten after about twice the learning time. Allowed values are in range 1..1000. The default value is 12 hours.

config_entries.label: Learning Time Offset Hours
config_entries.description: Time constant to estimate the VOC algorithm offset from the history in hours. Past events will be forgotten after about twice the learning time. Allowed values are in range 1..1000. The default value is 12 hour

config_entries.label: Std Initial
config_entries.description: Initial estimate for standard deviation. Lower value boosts events during initial learning period, but may result in larger device-todevice variations. Allowed values are in range 10..5000. The default value is 50.

components.name: Shelly Dimmer
components.description: The `shelly_dimmer` component adds support for the dimming and power-metering functionality that can be found the [Shelly Dimmer 2](https://shelly.cloud/knowledge-base/devices/shelly-dimmer-2/). The interaction with mains is done via an STM32 microcontroller that is automatically (when configured) flashed with an [open source firmware](https://github.com/jamesturton/shelly-dimmer-stm32). A detailed analysis of the Shelly Dimmer 2 hardware is given on [arendst/Tasmota#6914](https://github.com/arendst/Tasmota/issues/6914).

components.name: Sonoff D1 Dimmer
components.description: The `sonoff_d1` light platform creates a simple brightness-only light for the hardware found in [Sonoff D1 dimmer](https://itead.cc/product/sonoff-d1-smart-dimmer-switch/). Installations with Sonoff RM433 433MHz radio remotes are also supported. Use this component to integrate Sonoff D1 dimmer into ESPHome / Home Assistant ecosystem.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the light. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the light in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Restore Mode
config_entries.description: Control how the light attempts to restore state on bootup.

options.label: Always initialize the light as ON on bootup.
Attempt to restore state but initialize the light as OFF.
Attempt to restore state but initialize the light as ON.
Attempt to restore state and default to OFF if not possible to restore.
Attempt to restore state and default to ON.
Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to OFF.
Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to ON.

config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.description: The blue channel of the light.

config_entries.description: The primary brightness of the light; applies to all channels (both color and white) of the light.

config_entries.description: The brightness of the cold white channel. Cannot be used at the same time as *color_temperature*.

config_entries.label: Color Correct
config_entries.description: Apply a color correction to each color channel. This defines the maximum brightness of each channel. For example `[100%, 50%, 100%]` would set the green channel to be at most at 50% brightness.

config_entries.label: Color Temperature
config_entries.description: The color temperature (in [mireds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mired) or Kelvin) of the white channel.

config_entries.description: The green channel of the light.

config_entries.description: The initial state the light should be set to on bootup. This state will be applied when the state is **not** restored based on `restore_mode` (below).

config_entries.description: The ON/OFF state for the light.

config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.description: The highest dimmer value allowed. Use this to hard-limit light intensity for your setup. For some bulbs this parameter might be also useful to prevent flickering at high brightness values. Defaults to 100.

config_entries.label: Min Value
config_entries.description: The lowest dimmer value allowed. Acceptable value for your setup will depend on actual light bulbs installed and number of them. Start with the default value and check what will be the minimal brightness bulbs can render. Pay attention that for some dimmable LED lamps minimal turn-on brightness will be higher that the minimal achievable brightness if you just decrease it when lamp is already turned on. Defaults to 0.

config_entries.description: The [Power Supply](https://esphome.io/components/power_supply/) to connect to this light. When the light is turned on, the power supply will automatically be switched on too.

config_entries.label: Red
config_entries.description: The red channel of the light.

config_entries.label: Use Rm433 Remote
config_entries.description: Set to `True` if your setup uses Sonoff RM433 or any other radio remote control. Properly setting this parameter allows the platform to identify what to do with incoming UART commands. RF chip is known to catch random commands if not paired with a real remote (so called ghost commands). This problem is observed even with the stock firmware and most probably is a bug in the MCU firmware or in the RF chip firmware. Setting this to `False` instructs the platform to properly ignore such commands and thus prevent unexpected switches or light intensity changes.

config_entries.label: Warm White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the warm white channel. Cannot be used at the same time as *color_temperature*.

config_entries.label: White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the white channel.

components.name: SSD1306 OLED Display
components.description: The `ssd1306_i2c` display platform allows you to use SSD1306 ([datasheet](https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/datasheets/SSD1306.pdf), [Adafruit](https://www.adafruit.com/product/326)), SSD1305 ([datasheet](https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/datasheets/SSD1305.pdf)), SH1107 ([datasheet](https://cdn-learn.adafruit.com/assets/assets/000/094/580/original/SH1107_datasheet.pdf), [Adafruit](https://www.adafruit.com/product/4650)) and SH1106 ([datasheet](https://www.elecrow.com/download/SH1106%20datasheet.pdf), [electrodragon](https://www.electrodragon.com/product/1-3-12864-blue-oled-display-iicspi/)) displays with ESPHome. Note that this component is for displays that are connected via the [I²C Bus](https://esphome.io/components/i2c). If your SSD1306/SSD1305 or SH1106 is connected via the 4-Wire [SPI bus](https://esphome.io/components/spi), see [Over SPI](https://esphome.io/components/display/ssd1306#ssd1306-spi).

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: Manually specify the [I²C](https://esphome.io/components/i2c) address of the display. Defaults to 0x3C.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to re-draw the screen. Defaults to `1s`.

config_entries.label: Model
config_entries.description: The model of the display. Options are:

config_entries.label: Reset Pin
config_entries.description: The RESET pin. Defaults to not connected.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Auto Clear Enabled
config_entries.description: Whether to automatically clear the display data before each lambda call, or to keep the existing display content (must overwrite explicitly, e.g., only on data change). Defaults to `true` if a lambda or pages are configured, false otherwise.

config_entries.label: Brightness
config_entries.description: Set display brightness in %. Only can be used with SSD1305. Defaults to `100%`.

config_entries.label: Contrast
config_entries.description: Set display contrast in %. Defaults to `100%`.

config_entries.label: External Vcc
config_entries.description: Set this to true if you have the VCC pin connected to an external power supply. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Flip X
config_entries.description: Flip the horizontal axis on the screen. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Flip Y
config_entries.description: Flip the vertical axis on the screen. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Invert
config_entries.description: Invert all pixel state on the display. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: The lambda to use for rendering the content on the display. See [Display Rendering Engine](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-engine) for more information.

config_entries.label: Offset X
config_entries.description: Set this option if some horizontal pixel is missing. Numbers are only allowed between `0~128`. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Offset Y
config_entries.description: Set this option if some vertical pixel is missing. Numbers are only allowed between `0~128`. Defaults to `0`.

config_entries.label: Pages
config_entries.description: Show pages instead of a single lambda. See [Display Pages](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-pages).

config_entries.label: Rotation
config_entries.description: Set the rotation of the display. Everything you draw in `lambda:` will be rotated by this option. One of `0°` (default), `90°`, `180°`, `270°`.

components.name: SX126x Component
components.description: The SX126x component allows you to configure the SX1261, SX1262, SX1268 and LLCC68 transceivers ([datasheet](https://www.semtech.com/products/wireless-rf/lora-connect/sx1262#documentation)) in ESPHome. Transceivers are connected via the [SPI Bus](https://esphome.io/components/spi). Supported frequencies range from 150 MHz to 960 MHz, including the popular 315 MHz, 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz ISM bands. Supported modulations include LoRa, FSK, GFSK, MSK and GMSK. The SX126x component may be used as a platform for the [Packet Transport Component](https://esphome.io/components/packet_transport#packet-transport) component, enabling sensor data to be sent directly from one ESPHome node to another.

config_entries.label: Busy Pin
config_entries.description: Busy pin.

config_entries.label: Cs Pin
config_entries.description: SPI chip select pin.

config_entries.label: Dio1 Pin
config_entries.description: Digital IO pin 1.

config_entries.label: Frequency
config_entries.description: Frequency in Hz of the transceiver.

config_entries.label: Hw Version
config_entries.description: Valid values are `sx1261`, `sx1262`, `sx1268` or `llcc68`.

config_entries.label: Modulation
config_entries.description: Modulation can be `FSK` or `LORA`.

config_entries.label: Rf Switch
config_entries.description: Used to indicate if DIO2 controls an external RF switch.

config_entries.label: Rst Pin
config_entries.description: Reset pin.

config_entries.label: Bitrate
config_entries.description: Bit rate of the signal. Normally the inverse of the bit duration, eg 1 / 208 us is 4800 bps.

config_entries.label: Coding Rate
config_entries.description: Coding rate, values can be `CR_4_5`, `CR_4_6`, `CR_4_7` or `CR_4_8`. Defaults to `CR_4_5`.

config_entries.label: Crc Enable
config_entries.description: Enables a 16 bit CRC calculation/check. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Crc Initial
config_entries.description: Initial CRC value as a hex integer. Defaults to 0x1D0F.

config_entries.label: Crc Inverted
config_entries.description: Inverts the CRC if enabled. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Crc Polynomial
config_entries.description: CRC polynomial as a hex integer. Defaults to 0x1021.

config_entries.label: Crc Size
config_entries.description: Size of the CRC in bytes, either 1 or 2. Defaults to 2.

config_entries.label: Deviation
config_entries.description: Transmitter FSK frequency deviation, values range from 0 to 100 kHz. Defaults to `5kHz`.

config_entries.label: Pa Power
config_entries.description: Transmitter power, range is from -3 to 15 dBm when `hw_version` is `sx1261` and from -3 to 22 dBm otherwise.

config_entries.label: Pa Ramp
config_entries.description: Transmitter PA ramp, can be `10us`, `20us`, `40us`, `80us`, `200us`, `800us`, `1700us` or `3400us`.

config_entries.label: Payload Length
config_entries.description: Length of the packet. Maximum length is 255.

config_entries.label: Preamble Detect
config_entries.description: Minimum length of the preamble in bytes required by the receiver. Preamble detector is disabled if the size is 0 and its value capped at 4.

config_entries.label: Preamble Size
config_entries.description: Length of the preamble in bytes to be sent by the transmitter. This value should be larger than `preamble_detect` on the receive side to allow time for the receiver’s AFC and AGC to adjust.

config_entries.label: Rx Start
config_entries.description: Start the receiver automatically on boot or after transmitting.

config_entries.label: Shaping
config_entries.description: Transmitter data shaping can be `GAUSSIAN_BT_0_3`, `GAUSSIAN_BT_0_5`, `GAUSSIAN_BT_0_7`, `GAUSSIAN_BT_1_0` or `NONE`.

config_entries.label: Spreading Factor
config_entries.description: Spreading factor, values range from 6 to 12. Defaults to 7.

config_entries.label: Sync Value
config_entries.description: Synchronization bytes, list of 1 to 8 bytes, found after the preamble and before the payload.

config_entries.label: Tcxo Delay
config_entries.description: The time needed for the TCXO to stabilize.

config_entries.label: Tcxo Voltage
config_entries.description: Reference voltage of the external TCXO controlled by DIO3. If there is no TCXO this should be set to `NONE`. Values can be `1_6V`, `1_7V`, `1_8V`, `2_2V`, `2_4V`, `2_7V`, `3_0V`, `3_3V` or `NONE`.

components.name: SX127x Component
components.description: The SX127x component allows you to configure the SX1276, SX1277, SX1278 and SX1279 transceivers ([datasheet](https://www.semtech.com/products/wireless-rf/lora-connect/sx1278#documentation)) in ESPHome. Transceivers are connected via the [SPI Bus](https://esphome.io/components/spi). Supported frequencies range from 137 MHz to 1020 MHz, including the popular 315 MHz, 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz ISM bands. Supported modulations include LoRa, OOK, FSK, GFSK, MSK and GMSK. The SX127x component may be used as a platform for the [Packet Transport Component](https://esphome.io/components/packet_transport#packet-transport) component, enabling sensor data to be sent directly from one ESPHome node to another.

config_entries.label: Cs Pin
config_entries.description: SPI chip select pin.

config_entries.label: Dio0 Pin
config_entries.description: Digital IO pin 0.

config_entries.label: Frequency
config_entries.description: Frequency in Hz of the transceiver.

config_entries.label: Modulation
config_entries.description: Modulation can be `OOK`, `FSK` or `LORA`  `.

config_entries.label: Rst Pin
config_entries.description: Reset pin.

config_entries.label: Auto Cal
config_entries.description: Enable automatic image calibration on temperature changes. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Bitrate
config_entries.description: Bit rate of the signal. Required in packet mode and recommended in continuous mode. Normally the inverse of the bit duration, eg 1 / 208 us is 4800 bps.

config_entries.label: Bitsync
config_entries.description: Enables the receive bit synchronizer. Required in packet mode. Recommended in continuous mode, however if there is no preamble plus high noise it may be better to turn it off.

config_entries.label: Coding Rate
config_entries.description: Coding rate, values can be `CR_4_5`, `CR_4_6`, `CR_4_7` or `CR_4_8`. Defaults to `CR_4_5`.

config_entries.label: Crc Enable
config_entries.description: Enables a 16 bit CRC calculation/check in packet mode.

config_entries.label: Deviation
config_entries.description: Transmitter FSK frequency deviation, values range from 0 to 100 kHz. Defaults to `5kHz`.

config_entries.label: Pa Pin
config_entries.description: Transmitter output pin, can be `BOOST` or `RFO`.

config_entries.label: Pa Power
config_entries.description: Transmitter power, range is from 2 to 17 dBm when `pa_pin` is `BOOST` and 0 to 15 dBm when using `RFO`.

config_entries.label: Packet Mode
config_entries.description: In packet mode bytes are sent via the `send_packet` automation and received with the `on_packet` trigger. If not enabled continuous mode is used and raw data is sent and received on DIO2.

config_entries.label: Payload Length
config_entries.description: Length of the payload in packet mode. If not configured then the variable length packet format is used. Maximum length is 64.

config_entries.label: Preamble Detect
config_entries.description: Minimum length of the preamble in bytes required by the receiver. Preamble detector is disabled if the size is 0 and its value capped at 3.

config_entries.label: Preamble Errors
config_entries.description: Number of chip errors tolerated in the receiver.

config_entries.label: Preamble Polarity
config_entries.description: Polarity of the preamble, either 0xAA or 0x55.

config_entries.label: Preamble Size
config_entries.description: Length of the preamble, in bytes, to be sent by the transmitter. This value should be larger than `preamble_detect` on the receive side to allow time for the receiver’s AFC and AGC to adjust.

config_entries.label: Rx Floor
config_entries.description: When receiving OOK `rx_floor` should be set appropriately for your environment. If set too high (ie closer to 0) the radio will ignore everything. If set too low (ie closer to -128) too much noise will get through. When receiving FSK without a preamble configured `rx_floor` is used to trigger the receiver.

config_entries.label: Rx Start
config_entries.description: Start the receiver automatically on boot or after transmitting.

config_entries.label: Shaping
config_entries.description: Transmitter data shaping. In OOK can be `CUTOFF_BR_X_2`, `CUTOFF_BR_X_1` or `NONE`. In FSK can be `GAUSSIAN_BT_0_3`, `GAUSSIAN_BT_0_5`, `GAUSSIAN_BT_1_0` or `NONE`. Not recommended in continuous mode as the data on DIO2 must to be synchronized with the bit clock on DIO1.

config_entries.label: Spreading Factor
config_entries.description: Spreading factor, values range from 6 to 12. Defaults to 7.

config_entries.label: Sync Value
config_entries.description: Synchronization bytes, list of 1 to 8 bytes, found after the preamble and before the payload.

config_entries.label: Keypad

config_entries.label: Key Columns
config_entries.description: The number of keypad columns to use. This enables any number of the last 8 pins. So a value of 4 enables pins 8,9,10,11 to be used as the columns for the keypad matrix. This value must be between 1 and 8.

config_entries.label: Key Rows

config_entries.label: Debounce Time
config_entries.description: The debounce time is common to all IOs.

config_entries.label: Keys

components.name: Thermostat Climate Controller
components.description: The `thermostat` climate platform allows you to control a climate control system in much the same manner as a physical thermostat. Its operation is similar to the [Bang-Bang](https://esphome.io/components/climate/bang_bang/) controller; a sensor measures a value (the air temperature) and the controller will try to keep this value within a range defined by the set point(s). To do this, the controller can activate devices like a heating unit and/or a cooling unit to change the value observed by the sensor. When configured for both heating and cooling, it is essentially two [Bang-Bang](https://esphome.io/components/climate/bang_bang/) controllers in one; it differs, however, in that interaction with the thermostat component is nearly identical to that of a real thermostat.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the climate device. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the climate device in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Humidity Sensor
config_entries.description: If specified, this sensor is used to measure the current humidity. This may be used for humidity control; see [Humidity Control Actions](https://esphome.io/components/climate/thermostat#humidity-control-actions).

config_entries.label: Idle Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device should enter its idle state (not cooling, not heating).

config_entries.label: Min Idle Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration the idle action must be active before calling another climate action.

config_entries.label: Sensor
config_entries.description: The sensor that is used to measure the current temperature.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Action State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish climate device action changes to.

config_entries.label: Auto Mode
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device is placed into "auto" mode (it may both cool and heat as required). This mode is different from `heat_cool_mode` (above) in that it takes control of the set points away from the user; it's generally intended for exclusive use by automations.

config_entries.label: Cool Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device should enter cooling mode to decrease the current temperature.

config_entries.label: Cool Deadband
config_entries.description: The minimum temperature differential (temperature above the set point) before calling the cooling [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions). Defaults to 0.5 °C.

config_entries.label: Cool Mode
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device is placed into cool mode (it may cool as required, but not heat).

config_entries.label: Cool Overrun
config_entries.description: The minimum temperature differential (cooling beyond the set point) before calling the idle [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions). Defaults to 0.5 °C.

config_entries.label: Current Humidity State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish current humidity changes to.

config_entries.label: Current Temperature State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish current temperature changes to.

config_entries.label: Default Preset
config_entries.description: The name of the preset to use by default. Must match a preset as per [preset](https://esphome.io/components/climate/thermostat#thermostat-preset).

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Dry Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device should perform its drying (dehumidification) action. The thermostat controller does not trigger this action; it is invoked by `dry_mode` (see below).

config_entries.label: Dry Mode
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device is placed into dry mode (for dehumidification).

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Auto Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should be set to "auto" mode (the fan is controlled by the climate control system as required).

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive fan mode commands on.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Diffuse Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should direct its airflow over a broad area.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Focus Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should direct its airflow at a specific area.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode High Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should run at its maximum speed.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Low Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should run at its minimum speed.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Medium Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should run at an intermediate speed.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Middle Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should direct its airflow at an intermediate area.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Off Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should never run.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode On Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should run continuously.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode Quiet Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the fan should run at quiet speed.

config_entries.label: Fan Mode State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish fan mode changes to.

config_entries.label: Fan Only Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device should activate its fan only (but does not heat or cool). When `fan_only_cooling` is set to `false`, the thermostat controller immediately triggers this action when set to `fan_only_mode`  ; however, when `fan_only_cooling` is set to `true`, this action is called based on the upper target temperature (similar to `cool_action` above).

config_entries.label: Fan Only Action Uses Fan Mode Timer
config_entries.description: If set to `true`, the `fan_only_action` will share the same delay timer used for all `fan_mode` actions. The minimum fan switching delay is then determined by `min_fan_mode_switching_time` (see below). This is useful when `fan_only_action` controls the same physical fan as the `fan_mode` actions, common in forced-air HVAC systems.

config_entries.label: Fan Only Cooling
config_entries.description: If set to `true`, when in the `fan_only_mode` climate mode, the `fan_only_action` will only be called when the observed temperature exceeds the upper set point plus `cool_deadband`. When set to `false` (the default), `fan_only_action` is called immediately when `fan_only_mode` is activated, regardless of the current temperature or set points. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Fan Only Mode
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device is placed into fan-only mode (it may not heat or cool, but will activate its fan either immediately or, when `fan_only_cooling` is `true`, as needed based on the upper target temperature value).

config_entries.label: Fan With Cooling
config_entries.description: If set to `true`, `fan_only_action` will be called whenever `cool_action` is called. This is useful for forced-air systems where the fan typically runs with cooling. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Fan With Heating
config_entries.description: If set to `true`, `fan_only_action` will be called whenever `heat_action` is called. This is useful for forced-air systems where the fan typically runs with heating. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Heat Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device should enter heating mode to increase the current temperature.

config_entries.label: Heat Cool Mode
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device is placed into "heat/cool" mode (it may both cool and heat as required). If no action is desired, may be set to `true` to enable the mode without a related automation. Note that **both** `heat_action` **and** `cool_action` ([see above](https://esphome.io/components/climate/thermostat#heating-and-cooling-actions)) must be defined to enable this mode.

config_entries.label: Heat Deadband
config_entries.description: The minimum temperature differential (temperature below the set point) before calling the heating [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions). Defaults to 0.5 °C.

config_entries.label: Heat Mode
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device is placed into heat mode (it may heat as required, but not cool).

config_entries.label: Heat Overrun
config_entries.description: The minimum temperature differential (heating beyond the set point) before calling the idle [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#all-actions). Defaults to 0.5 °C.

config_entries.label: Humidity Control Dehumidify Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when dehumidification is required.

config_entries.label: Humidity Control Humidify Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when humidification is required.

config_entries.label: Humidity Control Off Action
config_entries.description: The action to call when (de)humidification should stop. This action is **required** when either of the above actions are configured.

config_entries.label: Humidity Hysteresis
config_entries.description: The maximum humidity differential (above/below the set point) before calling the respective humidity control [action](https://esphome.io/automations/actions#config-action). Defaults to 1%.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Max Cooling Run Time
config_entries.description: Duration after which `supplemental_cooling_action` will be called when cooling is active. Note that `supplemental_cooling_action` will be called repeatedly at an interval defined by this parameter, as well, enabling multiple stages of supplemental (auxiliary/emergency) cooling.

config_entries.label: Max Heating Run Time
config_entries.description: Duration after which `supplemental_heating_action` will be called when heating is active. Note that `supplemental_heating_action` will be called repeatedly at an interval defined by this parameter, as well, enabling multiple stages of supplemental (auxiliary/emergency) heating.

config_entries.label: Min Cooling Off Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration the cooling action must be disengaged before it may be engaged.

config_entries.label: Min Cooling Run Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration the cooling action must be engaged before it may be disengaged.

config_entries.label: Min Fan Mode Switching Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration any given fan mode must be active before it may be changed.

config_entries.label: Min Fanning Off Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration the fanning action must be disengaged before it may be engaged.

config_entries.label: Min Fanning Run Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration the fanning action must be engaged before it may be disengaged.

config_entries.label: Min Heating Off Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration the heating action must be disengaged before it may be engaged.

config_entries.label: Min Heating Run Time
config_entries.description: Minimum duration the heating action must be engaged before it may be disengaged.

config_entries.label: Mode Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive climate device mode commands on.

config_entries.label: Mode State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish climate device mode changes to.

config_entries.label: Off Mode
config_entries.description: The action to call when the climate device is placed into "off" mode (it is completely disabled).

config_entries.label: Preset

components.name: Time Based Cover
components.description: The `time_based` cover platform allows you to create covers with position control that do not have any position feedback. The state of the cover is thus always an assumed one, the current position is approximated with the time the cover has been moving in a direction. The state of the cover can be restored at node reboot.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the cover. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the cover in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cover/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cover/#device-class) for a list of available options.

config_entries.label: Close Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to be closed.

config_entries.label: Close Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time it takes the cover to close from the fully-open state.

config_entries.label: Open Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed when the remote requests the cover to be opened.

config_entries.label: Open Duration
config_entries.description: The amount of time it takes the cover to open up from the fully-closed state.

config_entries.label: Stop Action
config_entries.description: The action that should be performed to stop the cover when the remote requests the cover to be stopped or when the cover has been opening/closing for the given durations.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Assumed State
config_entries.description: Whether the true state of the cover is not known. This will make the Home Assistant frontend show buttons for both OPEN and CLOSE actions, instead of hiding or disabling one of them. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Has Built In Endstop
config_entries.description: Indicates that the cover has built in end stop detectors. In this configuration the `stop_action` is not performed when the open or close time is completed and if the cover is commanded to open or close the corresponding actions will be performed without checking current state. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Manual Control
config_entries.description: For covers with manual external controls. With this configuration if the cover is commanded to open or close the corresponding actions will be performed even if the current state fully open or fully closed matches desired state, then `stop_action` will be called after the full duration of the action elapses. The current state will then be relearned upon completion. It's recommended to set `assumed_state` to true so the cover control button aren't disabled in the interface. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Mqtt Json State Payload
config_entries.description: When set to `true`, state changes will be published only to the `state_topic` as a single JSON object per state change. Example: ```json { "state": "open", "position": 100, "tilt": 50 } ``` When `false`, individual values are published to the `state_topic`, `position_state_topic`, and `tilt_state_topic` separately. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Position Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive cover position commands on.

config_entries.label: Position State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish cover position changes to. Not valid if `mqtt_json_state_payload` is set to `true`.

config_entries.label: Tilt Command Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to receive cover tilt commands on.

config_entries.label: Tilt State Topic
config_entries.description: The topic to publish cover cover tilt state changes to. Not valid if `mqtt_json_state_payload` is set to `true`.

components.name: TX20/TX23 Wind Speed/Direction Sensor
components.description: The `tx20` sensor platform allows you to use your TX20/TX23 wind direction and speed sensors with ESPHome. The only required pin is the black or brown cable (which is used to transmit data.) The red cable should be connected to VCC (3.3V), green initiates the data transfer when connected to GND and should therefore be directly connected to GND and the yellow cable should be always connected to ground. The difference from the TX20 to the TX23 seems to be that the green cable does not matter any more and the wind sensor is just sending a datagram every 2 seconds - pretty much the same as when the green cable was connected to GND in the TX20.
