components.name: UART Bus
components.description: UART is a common serial protocol for many devices. For example, when uploading a binary to your ESP you have probably used UART to access the chip. UART (or for Arduino often also called Serial) usually consists of 2 pins:

config_entries.label: Baud Rate
config_entries.description: The baud rate of the UART bus.

config_entries.label: Debug
config_entries.description: Log UART traffic to the ESPHome log for troubleshooting. Bare `debug:` enables hex logging with sensible defaults.

config_entries.label: Direction
config_entries.description: Which side of the bus to log. Defaults to `BOTH`.

config_entries.label: Debug Prefix
config_entries.description: Prefix prepended to every debug log line. Useful when multiple UART buses log at the same time.

config_entries.label: Dummy Receiver
config_entries.description: Capture incoming bytes even when no UART device component is bound to the bus. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: After
config_entries.description: When to flush accumulated bytes to the log.

config_entries.label: Bytes
config_entries.description: Flush after this many bytes have been accumulated. Defaults to 150.

config_entries.label: Timeout
config_entries.description: Flush after no bytes have been seen for this long. Defaults to `100ms`.

config_entries.label: Delimiter
config_entries.description: Flush as soon as this byte sequence is seen in the stream.

config_entries.label: Flow Control Pin
config_entries.description: ESP32 only. The pin used to for hardware RS485 flow control. Use of this setting enables half-duplex mode. Use the full pin schema and set `inverted: true` to invert logic levels.

config_entries.label: Rx Pin
config_entries.description: The pin to receive data on from the ESP's perspective. Use the full pin schema and set `inverted: true` to invert logic levels. Not supported by host platform.

config_entries.label: Tx Pin
config_entries.description: The pin to send data to from the ESP's perspective. Use the full pin schema and set `inverted: true` to invert logic levels. Not supported by host platform.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for this UART hub if you need multiple UART hubs.

config_entries.label: Data Bits
config_entries.description: The number of data bits used on the UART bus. Options: 5 to 8. Defaults to 8.

config_entries.label: Flush Timeout
config_entries.description: ESP32 only. The maximum time to wait for the TX FIFO to drain when `flush()` is called. If the TX FIFO does not drain within this time, `flush()` returns a `TIMEOUT` result. When not set, `flush()` waits indefinitely.

config_entries.label: Parity
config_entries.description: The parity used on the UART bus. Options: `NONE`, `EVEN`, `ODD`. Defaults to `NONE`.

config_entries.label: Port
config_entries.description: Host platform only. Unix style name of the port to use.

config_entries.label: Rx Buffer Size
config_entries.description: The size of the buffer used for receiving UART messages. Increase if you use an integration that needs to read big payloads from UART. Defaults to `256`.

config_entries.label: Rx Full Threshold
config_entries.description: ESP32 only. After receiving this number of bytes, the data becomes available for processing. The default is calculated at compilation time to be approximately ten milliseconds (about 8 bytes at 9600 baud, 114 bytes at 115200 baud).

config_entries.label: Rx Timeout
config_entries.description: ESP32 only. This value specifies a number of bytes used to determine the duration of the timeout. The duration of the timeout is based on the amount of time it would take to receive this number of bytes. In other words, for a given value and baud rate, doubling the baud rate will halve the duration of the timeout. After the timeout has elapsed, the data becomes available for processing. Defaults to `2`.

config_entries.label: Stop Bits
config_entries.description: The number of stop bits to send. Options: 1, 2. Defaults to 1.

components.description: The `uptime` text sensor provides a human-readable representation the time since. The elements can be separated by a custom string, and more significant elements will be omitted if they are zero. For example, if the uptime is 1 day, 2 hours, 3 minutes, and 4 seconds, the sensor will report `1d2h3m4s` with the default configuration. By default leading zero elements will be trimmed from the output, e.g. if the uptime is 0 days, 0 hours, 3 minutes, and 0 seconds, the sensor will report `3m0s`. config_entries.description: Maximum number of concurrent USB transfer requests. Range: 1-32. Defaults to `16`. Increase this value for high-throughput devices (e.g., USB UART at 115200+ baud) if you see "All X transfer slots in use" errors.

components.name: Waveshare E-Paper Display
components.description: The `waveshare_epaper` display platform allows you to use some E-Paper displays sold by [Waveshare](https://www.waveshare.com/product/displays/e-paper.htm) with ESPHome. The 2.13" [TTGO module](https://github.com/lewisxhe/TTGO-EPaper-Series) and the [Waveshare Cloud Module](https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/2.13inch_e-Paper_Cloud_Module) with an ESP32 on the board are supported as well. Depending on your specific revision of the TTGO board you might need to try out the `-b73` or `-b1` version (see below). The 1.54" [Good Display gdew0154m09](https://www.good-display.com/product/206.html) as used in the [M5Stack Core Ink](https://shop.m5stack.com/products/m5stack-esp32-core-ink-development-kit1-54-elnk-display) is also supported. Similar modules sold by other vendors might also work but not have been tested yet.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval to re-draw the screen. Defaults to `1s`, use `never` to only manually update the screen via `component.update`.

config_entries.label: Model
config_entries.description: The model of the E-Paper display. Options are:

options.label: GoodDisplay gdew0154m09, as used in the M5Stack Core Ink
13.3in, with the K model, 960x680, B/W rendering only
T5_V2.3 tested. Also works for Wemos D1 Mini ePaper Shield 2.13 1.0.0 "LOLIN"
T5_V2.3 with DKE group display (DEPG0213BN) tested
2.13in V2 display (Pico e-Paper 2.13v2 and Cloud Module)
currently not working with the HAT Rev 2.1 version
2.9in V2 display, but with different initialization and full/partial display refresh management than `2.90inv2`
7.3in 7-color display (black, white, red, yellow, blue, green, and orange)
display with version sticker '(C)' on the back, B/W rendering only
Can't use with an ESP8266 as it runs out of RAM
GooDisplay GDEW029T5, as used on the AdaFruit MagTag and Pimoroni Badger
GooDisplay GDEY029t94, as used in the monochrome 2.9inch display from seeedstudio

config_entries.label: Busy Pin
config_entries.description: The BUSY pin. Defaults to not connected.

config_entries.label: Cs Pin
config_entries.description: The CS pin.

config_entries.label: Dc Pin
config_entries.description: The DC pin.

config_entries.label: Reset Pin
config_entries.description: The RESET pin. Defaults to not connected. Make sure you pull this pin high (by connecting it to 3.3V with a resistor) if not connected to a GPIO pin. The 2.13" B74 and V2 display variants require the reset pin.

config_entries.label: Spi Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID of the [SPI Component](https://esphome.io/components/spi) if you want to use multiple SPI buses.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Auto Clear Enabled
config_entries.description: Whether to automatically clear the display data before each lambda call, or to keep the existing display content (must overwrite explicitly, e.g., only on data change). Defaults to `true` if a lambda or pages are configured, false otherwise.

config_entries.label: Full Update Every
config_entries.description: E-Paper displays have two modes of switching to the next image: A partial update that only changes the pixels that have changed and a full update mode that first clears the entire display and then re-draws the image. The former is much quicker and nicer, but every so often a full update needs to happen because artifacts accumulate. On the `1.54in`, `1.54inv2`, `2.13in`, `2.13inv2`, `2.90in`, `2.90inv2`, `7.50inV2p` and `gdew029t5` models, you have the option to only do a full-redraw every x-th time using this option. Defaults to `30` on the described models and a full update for all other models.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: The lambda to use for rendering the content on the display. See [Display Rendering Engine](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-engine) for more information.

config_entries.label: Pages
config_entries.description: Show pages instead of a single lambda. See [Display Pages](https://esphome.io/components/display#display-pages).

config_entries.label: Reset Duration
config_entries.description: Duration for the display reset operation. Defaults to `200ms`. Setting this value to `2ms` may resolve issues with newer e-Paper Driver modules (e.g. Rev 2.1).

config_entries.label: Rotation
config_entries.description: Set the rotation of the display. Everything you draw in `lambda:` will be rotated by this option. One of `0°` (default), `90°`, `180°`, `270°`.

components.name: Web Server Component
components.description: The `web_server` component creates a simple web server on the node that can be accessed through any browser and a simple [REST API](https://esphome.io/web-api#api-rest). Please note that enabling this component will take up *a lot* of memory and may decrease stability, especially on ESP8266.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Auth
config_entries.description: Enables a simple *Digest* authentication with username and password.

config_entries.label: Password
config_entries.description: The password to check for authentication.

config_entries.label: Username
config_entries.description: The username to use for authentication.

config_entries.label: Compression
config_entries.description: The compression algorithm used for embedded web assets when `local` is enabled. Options are `gzip` or `br` (Brotli). Brotli provides smaller embedded web assets (~10% smaller than gzip), but some browsers only support Brotli over HTTPS connections. Since ESPHome devices typically serve over HTTP, gzip is recommended for maximum compatibility. Defaults to `gzip`.

config_entries.label: Css Include
config_entries.description: Path to local file to be included in web server index page. Contents of this file will be served as `/0.css` and used as CSS stylesheet by internal webserver. Useful when building device without internet access, where you want to use built-in AP and webserver.

config_entries.label: Css Url

components.name: WiFi Component
components.description: This core ESPHome component sets up WiFi connections to access points for you. You need to have a network configuration (either Wifi or Ethernet) or ESPHome will fail in the config validation stage. You also can't have both Wifi and Ethernet setup in same time (even if your ESP has both wired).

config_entries.label: Ssid
config_entries.description: The SSID or WiFi network name.

config_entries.label: Password
config_entries.description: The password to present to the authentication server. For EAP-TLS this password may be set to decrypt to private key instead.

config_entries.label: Fallback Access Point
config_entries.description: Bring up an access point on the device when it can't reach the configured WiFi network. Pair with `captive_portal:` or `web_server:` so the user can connect to the AP and reconfigure WiFi from a phone.

config_entries.label: SSID
config_entries.description: Name of the access point to create. Leave empty to use the device name.

config_entries.label: Password
config_entries.description: Password for the access point. Leave empty for an open network.

config_entries.label: Channel
config_entries.description: 2.4GHz channel the AP should operate on (1-14). Defaults to 1.

config_entries.label: AP Timeout
config_entries.description: Time without a station connection before the fallback access point comes up. Set to `0s` to disable automatic startup. Defaults to `90s`.

config_entries.label: Manual IP
config_entries.description: Manually set the IP options for the AP. Same fields as the station-side `manual_ip:`.

config_entries.label: Static IP
config_entries.description: The static IP of the AP.

config_entries.label: Gateway
config_entries.description: The gateway of the AP network.

config_entries.label: Subnet
config_entries.description: The subnet of the AP network.

config_entries.label: DNS 1
config_entries.description: The main DNS server for the AP.

config_entries.label: DNS 2
config_entries.description: The backup DNS server for the AP.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Band Mode
config_entries.description: Only on `esp32-c5`. Controls which WiFi frequency band the device uses. Possible values are `AUTO` (use both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), `2.4GHZ` (2.4 GHz only), and `5GHZ` (5 GHz only). If not specified, it defaults to `AUTO`.

config_entries.label: Domain
config_entries.description: Set the domain of the node hostname used for uploading. For example, if it's set to `.local`, all uploads will be sent to `<HOSTNAME>.local`. Defaults to `.local`.

config_entries.label: Eap
config_entries.description: See [Enterprise Authentication](https://esphome.io/components/wifi#eap).

config_entries.label: Enable Btm
config_entries.description: Only on `esp32`. Enable 802.11v BSS Transition Management support.

config_entries.label: Enable On Boot
config_entries.description: If enabled, the WiFi interface will be enabled on boot. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Enable Rrm
config_entries.description: Only on `esp32`. Enable 802.11k Radio Resource Management support.

config_entries.label: Fast Connect
config_entries.description: If enabled, directly connects to WiFi network without doing a full scan first. This can significantly improve connection times (thus reducing power consumption). Defaults to `off`. The downside is that this option connects to the first network the ESP sees, even if that network is very far away and better ones are available. If multiple networks are configured, the last successfully connected one is tested first. In case it fails, all networks are then tested one after the other in their declared order, starting with the first one in the list. > [!NOTE] > While `fast_connect` skips the initial scan, if the connection attempt fails, ESPHome will still perform a scan > to find available networks. For hidden networks, use `hidden: true` on the network configuration (see > [Connecting to Multiple Networks](https://esphome.io/components/wifi#wifi-networks)) to ensure the device always connects without scanning. > Be aware that marking networks as hidden prevents ESPHome from finding the best access point to connect to, > so the device may not connect to the AP with the best signal strength.

config_entries.label: Manual Ip
config_entries.description: Manually configure the static IP of the node when using this network. Note that when using different static IP addresses on each network, it is required to set `use_address`, as ESPHome cannot infer to which network the node is connected.

config_entries.label: Gateway
config_entries.description: The gateway of the local network.

config_entries.label: Static Ip
config_entries.description: The static IP of your node.

config_entries.label: Subnet
config_entries.description: The subnet of the local network.

config_entries.label: Dns1
config_entries.description: The main DNS server to use.

config_entries.label: Dns2
config_entries.description: The backup DNS server to use.

config_entries.label: Min Auth Mode
config_entries.description: Only on `esp32` and `esp8266`. Sets the minimum WiFi authentication mode that the device will accept when connecting to access points. This controls the weakest encryption your device will allow. Possible values are:

options.label: Allows WPA, WPA2, and WPA3 networks (least secure, uses TKIP encryption with known vulnerabilities)
Allows WPA2 and WPA3 networks (recommended, uses AES encryption)
Only allows WPA3 networks (most secure, ESP32 only)

config_entries.label: Networks
config_entries.description: Configure multiple WiFi networks to connect to, the best one that is reachable will be connected to. See [Connecting to Multiple Networks](https://esphome.io/components/wifi#wifi-networks).

config_entries.label: Gateway
config_entries.description: The gateway of the local network.

config_entries.label: Static Ip
config_entries.description: The static IP of your node.

config_entries.label: Subnet
config_entries.description: The subnet of the local network.

config_entries.label: Dns1
config_entries.description: The main DNS server to use.

config_entries.label: Dns2
config_entries.description: The backup DNS server to use.

config_entries.label: Output Power
config_entries.description: The amount of TX power for the WiFi interface from 8.5dB to 20.5dB. Default for ESP8266 is 20dB, 20.5dB might cause unexpected restarts.

config_entries.label: Passive Scan
config_entries.description: If enabled, then the device will perform WiFi scans in a passive fashion. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Post Connect Roaming
config_entries.description: Enable basic post-connect roaming for stationary devices. After connecting to a non-hidden network, the device will periodically check for better access points with the same SSID and switch if one is found with significantly better signal (+10 dB). This helps devices recover from scenarios where they connect to a suboptimal AP (e.g., after an AP reboot or site power loss). Automatically disabled if `enable_btm` or `enable_rrm` is enabled. See [Post-Connect Roaming](https://esphome.io/components/wifi#wifi-post_connect_roaming). Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Power Save Mode
config_entries.description: The power save mode for the WiFi interface. See [Power Save Mode](https://esphome.io/components/wifi#wifi-power_save_mode)

config_entries.label: Reboot Timeout
config_entries.description: The amount of time to wait before rebooting when no WiFi connection exists. Can be disabled by setting this to `0s`, but note that the low level IP stack currently seems to have issues with WiFi where a full reboot is required to get the interface back working. Defaults to `15min`. Does not apply when in access point mode.

config_entries.label: Use Address
config_entries.description: Manually override what address to use to connect to the ESP. Defaults to auto-generated value. Example, if you have changed your static IP and want to flash OTA to the previously configured IP address.

config_entries.label: Use Psram
config_entries.description: For ESP32 only, requests that the WiFi libraries try to allocate memory from PSRAM. Defaults to `false`. Requires PSRAM to be configured.

components.name: WireGuard Component
components.description: [WireGuard®](https://www.wireguard.org/) is an extremely simple yet fast and modern VPN that utilizes state-of-the-art cryptography. This component uses a **custom** implementation not developed by original authors and currently available for ESP32, ESP8266 and BK72xx microcontrollers *only*.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: The local VPN address of the device. If you intend to upload firmwares through the VPN link you probably need to copy this value to the `use_address` parameter of the [Wifi](https://esphome.io/components/wifi/).

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: How often to check the connection status and the latest handshake value. Default to `10s`.

config_entries.label: Peer Endpoint
config_entries.description: The hostname of the remote peer.

config_entries.label: Peer Public Key
config_entries.description: The public key of the remote peer.

config_entries.label: Private Key
config_entries.description: The private key of the device.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Netmask
config_entries.description: The netmask for the configured address. Default to `255.255.255.255`. See section [Static routes and outgoing connections](https://esphome.io/components/wireguard#wireguard-static-routes) if outgoing connections are expected to transit through the VPN link (e.g. with [Mqtt](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/) to a remote MQTT broker).

config_entries.label: Peer Allowed Ips
config_entries.description: A list of networks in CIDR notation (*IP/mask*) to be allowed through the tunnel. Any host (`0.0.0.0/0`  ) will be allowed if this parameter is omitted. The device own `address/32` is always added by default to this list. See section [Static routes and outgoing connections](https://esphome.io/components/wireguard#wireguard-static-routes) if outgoing connections are expected to transit through the VPN link (e.g. with [Mqtt](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/) to a remote MQTT broker).

config_entries.label: Peer Persistent Keepalive
config_entries.description: The amount of time after which a *keepalive* packet is sent through the tunnel. By default this feature is disabled (`0s`  ). If there are NATs or firewalls between the device and the remote peer set this value to something like `25s`.

config_entries.label: Peer Port
config_entries.description: The port where remote peer is listening on. The WireGuard® default is `51820`.

config_entries.label: Peer Preshared Key
config_entries.description: The chosen pre-shared key between local device and remote peer.

config_entries.label: Reboot Timeout
config_entries.description: The amount of time to wait before rebooting the device when the remote peer is unreachable. Can be disabled by setting this to `0s`. Default to `15min`.

config_entries.label: Require Connection To Proceed
config_entries.description: Set to `true` to wait for the remote peer to be up before continuing to boot the device. Default to `false`. This can be used to delay the initialization of components that use the VPN tunnel as long as the VPN isn't ready. For example if you are using [Mqtt](https://esphome.io/components/mqtt/) to reach a remote broker you may experience boot freeze just after the setup of MQTT because it waits for the broker to be reachable, but the connection cannot be established until the VPN link is active too. To bypass such deadlock set this parameter to `true` in order to not initialize MQTT until the remote peer is up.

components.name: Xiaomi Mijia BLE Sensors
components.description: The `xiaomi_ble` sensor platform lets you track the output of Xiaomi Bluetooth Low Energy devices using the [Esp32 Ble Tracker](https://esphome.io/components/esp32_ble_tracker/). This component will track, for example, the temperature, humidity, moisture, conductivity, illuminance, formaldehyde, mosquito tablet and battery level of the device every time the sensor sends out a BLE broadcast. Contrary to other implementations, `xiaomi_ble` listens passively to advertisement packets and does not pair with the device. Hence ESPHome has no impact on battery life. Thus, if you only use such sensors, you can safely set `scan_parameters.active: false` in `esp32_ble_tracker` configuration, to save from spamming your RF environment with useless scan requests.

components.name: Xiaomi Miscale Sensors
components.description: The `xiaomi_miscale` sensor platform lets you track the output of Xiaomi Bluetooth Low Energy devices using the [Esp32 Ble Tracker](https://esphome.io/components/esp32_ble_tracker/). This component will track, for example, the weight of the device every time the sensor sends out a BLE broadcast. Contrary to other implementations, `xiaomi_miscale` listens passively to advertisement packets and does not pair with the device. Hence ESPHome has no impact on battery life.

config_entries.description: Clear the impedance information if a weight reading without impedance is received. Defaults to `false`. **Only available on MiScale2** Useful in the example below if a person steps onto the scale without waiting for the complete measurement. Without setting the flag the impedance reading of the measurement before will be used for the currently measured person.

components.name: Zigbee End Device
components.description: The `zigbee` component allows exposing supported ESPHome components over a Zigbee network to Home Assistant via **Zigbee2MQTT** or **ZHA**. Due to the limitations of the Zigbee protocol, only basic properties are exposed. Additional properties must be configured manually in Home Assistant. Each ESPHome entity consumes one Zigbee endpoint. Single endpoint requires ZHA or at least Zigbee2MQTT 2.8.0. For older versions of Zigbee2MQTT use multiple endpoints. Spaces in names require ZHA or at least Zigbee2MQTT 2.8.0. For older versions of Zigbee2MQTT do not use spaces. The maximum number of supported endpoints is eight.

config_entries.label: Id
config_entries.description: The ID to use for this `zigbee` component.

config_entries.label: Ieee802154 Vendor Oui
config_entries.description: Sets the Vendor Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI). This allows replacing Nordic Semiconductor's default company ID with your own. The value must be a 24-bit integer in the range `0x000000` to `0xFFFFFF`. Alternatively, set to `random` to generate a new random OUI on every firmware compilation. This is useful during development to force the coordinator (ZHA/Z2M) to recognize the device as new after firmware updates.

config_entries.label: Power Source
config_entries.description: Indicates what kind of power the device uses. Affects sleep behavior. One of `UNKNOWN`, `MAINS_SINGLE_PHASE`, `MAINS_THREE_PHASE`, `BATTERY`, `DC_SOURCE`, `EMERGENCY_MAINS_CONST`, or `EMERGENCY_MAINS_TRANSF`. Defaults to `DC_SOURCE`.

config_entries.label: Wipe On Boot
config_entries.description: Erases all non-volatile memory data on boot, including Zigbee network pairing and preferences (e.g., last switch state). One of:

options.label: Erase data only on first boot after flashing new firmware, then preserve.

ESPHome tries to automatically infer the time zone string based on the time zone of the computer that is running ESPHome, but this might not always be accurate. Not available on nRF52 platforms.

components.name: Z-Wave Proxy
components.description: The `zwave_proxy` component allows proxying of Z-Wave data frames between a [Z-Wave Modem SoC](https://www.silabs.com/wireless/z-wave/800-series-modem-soc) and [Z-Wave JS](https://zwave-js.github.io/zwave-js/) via ESPHome's [Api](https://esphome.io/components/api/) over the [Wifi](https://esphome.io/components/wifi/) or [Ethernet](https://esphome.io/components/ethernet/). This allows for more flexibility when placing your Z-Wave hardware within your home.

components.name: OTA Updates
components.description: Over-the-Air firmware updates. When `ota:` is configured as a bare mapping (no `- platform:` list — the legacy form), ESPHome implicitly uses the `esphome` platform. Modern configs select a platform explicitly: available platforms are `esphome`, `http_request`, `web_server`, `zephyr_mcumgr`.

components.name: Time Source
components.description: Time source / real-time clock for the device. When `time:` is configured as a bare mapping (no `- platform:` list — the legacy form), ESPHome implicitly uses the `homeassistant` platform. Modern configs select a platform explicitly: available platforms are `bm8563`, `ds1307`, `gps`, `homeassistant`, `host`, `pcf85063`, `pcf8563`, `rx8130`, `sntp`, `zigbee`.
